STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.claim: Its themes include God's power over nature and repeated warnings of punishment on earth or in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:intro/r6.anchor: references to God’s Power over the natural world (vv. 66–70), repeated warnings to human beings about the coming of Divine Punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Section III invites Jews and Quraysh to the Qur’an's natural straight path, contrasts the fates of acceptance and rejection, rebukes those blind to signs who demand punishment, and alludes to God's practice of punishing nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: both the Jews and the Idolaters of the Quraysh are invited to profess faith in the Qur’ ān

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word ṭā’ir literally means bird; because Arabs sought omens and the future from birds, it came to mean fate or future.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: since the Arabs used it as an omen and portent

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: At Judgment no soul bears another's burden; each person sees and carries the burden of their own deeds.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Every person will observe his deeds and carry their burden alone

BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r6.claim: The obligation to account for the deed is universal, applying to every accountable believer or unbeliever, male or female, learned or ignorant, ruler or subject, free or enslaved.
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r6.anchor: مكلف مؤمنا كان أو كافرا ذكرا أو أنثى عالما أو أميا

BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r7.claim: The person's bird means the lifetime of chosen deeds allotted to him by decree, as if it flew from the unseen nest; its attachment to his neck pictures its permanent bond to him.
BURSEVI:v5p106#2/r7.anchor: أي : عمره الصادر عنه باختياره حسبما قدر له كأنه طار إليه

BURSEVI:v5p107/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107/r1.speaker: أسئلة المقحمة
BURSEVI:v5p107/r1.claim: The neck is specified because it bears identifying marks and necklaces, both adornments and disgrace; Arabic idiom places binding obligations on one's neck.
BURSEVI:v5p107/r1.anchor: قال في "الأسئلة المقحمة" : كيف خص العنق بإلزامه الطائر

BURSEVI:v5p107/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107/r2.speaker: حياة الحيوان
BURSEVI:v5p107/r2.claim: The work compares an ugly trait clinging to a dove like its collar, which never leaves it, with each person's deed remaining attached like a necklace or shackle.
BURSEVI:v5p107/r2.anchor: وفي "حياة الحيوان" : أنهم قالوا تقلدها طوق الحمامة

BURSEVI:v5p107/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107/r3.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p107/r3.claim: The esoteric commentary says the bird is each person's pre-eternal allotment of happiness or misery and all decreed states and deeds; it attached at emergence from nonexistence and remains through life, death, and resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p107/r3.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : يشير إلى ما طار لكل إنسان

BURSEVI:v5p107/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p107/r4.claim: The book brought forth at resurrection contains every deed, down to the smallest trace; it was folded and is now open for its owner to see.
BURSEVI:v5p107/r4.anchor: مسطورا فيه عمله نقيرا وقطميرا وهو مفعول نخرج الإنسان

BURSEVI:v5p107/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p107/r5.speaker: الحسن
BURSEVI:v5p107/r5.claim: Al-Hasan says two angels record good deeds on the right and bad ones on the left; after death the scroll is folded and kept with the person in the grave until the resurrection.
BURSEVI:v5p107/r5.anchor: قال الحسن : بسطت لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان فهما عن يمينك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r1.claim: “Every human” is syntactically like “everything” above and refers to each morally accountable person.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r2.claim: A person’s ṭāʾir is the voluntary deed apportioned to him, good or evil, as though it flew to him from the hidden nest of destiny.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r2.anchor: أي عمله الصادر منه باختياره حسبما قدر له خير أكان أو شرا كأنه طار إليه من عش الغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r3.claim: The bird metaphor comes from Arabs’ divination: a bird released on a journey was lucky if it passed left to right (sāniḥ) and unlucky right to left (bāriḥ), so deeds and decree became figurative “birds.”
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r3.anchor: كانوا يتفاءلون بالطير ويسمونه زجرا فإذا سافروا ومر بهم طير زجروه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas interprets ṭāʾir here as a person’s deed; Mujahid is also reported to hold this interpretation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r4.anchor: وتفسيره بالعمل هنا مروي عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r5.claim: Mujahid likewise interprets ṭāʾir as the person’s deed, according to a report in al-Bayhaqi’s Shuʿab al-Iman.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r5.anchor: ورواه البيهقي في شعب الإيمان عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation makes ṭāʾir one’s primordial allotted share, assigned according to what one merits in God’s eternal knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r6.anchor: وفسره بعضهم بما وقع للعبد في القسمة الأزلية الواقعة حسب استحقاقه في العلم الأزلي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r7.claim: “In his neck” pictures an inescapable, permanent attachment, like a collar or shackle; the neck is visible and can stand for the whole person.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r8.speaker: حذيفة بن أسيد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r8.claim: A report from the Prophet says an angel forms the fetus after four months, records its features, happiness or misery, lifespan, provision, trials, and deeds, then hangs its book at its neck until God’s decree.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p31#2/r8.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r1.claim: The fetal-record report appears to make “neck” literal and ṭāʾir the written book; Anas is explicitly reported to interpret it that way, and the author accepts sound reports while deferring their manner.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r1.anchor: وأن الطائر عبارة عن كتاب الذي كتب فيه ما كتب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r2.claim: Mujahid says every newborn has a leaf at its neck recording whether the child is blessed or wretched, supporting an unrestricted reading of “every human”; the verse’s ending seems to limit it to the accountable.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r2.anchor: أخرجه أبو داؤد في كتاب القدر وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r3.speaker: مجاهد والحسن وأبو رجاء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r3.claim: Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Abu Rajaʾ read ṭāʾir as ṭayr; another reading gives sukūn to the nūn in ʿunuq.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r4.claim: The emerging book is the person’s record of deeds for the reckoning; its accusative can be the object of “bring forth” or a circumstantial description of the omitted object, the bird.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r4.anchor: والبعث للحساب ﴿ كتابا ﴾ ( هي صحيفة عمله

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r5.speaker: يعقوب ومجاهد وابن محيصن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r5.claim: Yaʿqub, Mujahid, and Ibn Muhaysin read the verb actively with “book” accusative as a circumstantial phrase, taking the bird as its subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r5.anchor: ويعضد ذلك قراءة يعقوب ومجاهد وابن محيصن

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r6.claim: Abu Jaʿfar’s passive reading with accusative “book” also supports a circumstantial construction; other variants make “book” the passive subject or active subject.

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r7.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb’s reading says each person’s bird “reads it on Judgment Day as a book,” explicitly identifying the bird with the record.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r7.anchor: عن هرون قال في قراءة أبي بن كعب

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r8.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر والجحدري والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAmir, Abu Jaʿfar, al-Jahdari, and in one report al-Hasan read “it is delivered to him,” with a passive intensive form.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر والجحدري والحسن بخلاف عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.claim: Al-Hasan likens the record to a person’s open ledger kept by two noble angels, one on each side; it is folded at death, placed on the neck in the grave, then brought out at resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p32#2/r1.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن الحسن أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r9.claim: The verse about each person's record has an earlier mystical interpretation in this commentary, which Alusi refers readers back to rather than repeating.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p51/r9.anchor: وكل إنسان ألرمناه طائره في عنقه ) الآية تقدم ما يصلح أن يكون من باب الإشارة فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says a person's bird is their deed and decree, which remains with them wherever they go.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: عمله وما قدر عليه فهو ملازمه أينما كان.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r2.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say a person's good and evil accompany them until reckoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r2.anchor: وقال الكلبي ومقاتل: خيره وشره معه لا يفارقه حتى يحاسبه به.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r3.claim: Hasan interprets the bird as one's good fortune and ill fortune.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r4.claim: Mujahid says every newborn has a paper at the neck marked blessed or wretched.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r4.anchor: وعن مجاهد: ما من مولود إلا في عنقه ورقة مكتوب فيها شقي أو سعيد.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r5.speaker: أهل المعاني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r5.claim: Exegetes of linguistic meaning take the bird as God's decree about a person's deeds and final felicity or misery, invoking Arab augury from birds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r5.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: أراد بالطائر ما قضى الله عليه أنه عامله وما هو صائر إليه من سعادة أو شقاوة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة والقتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda and al-Qutaybi take it as one's share of good or evil, from an expression for an arrow's allotted share; the neck represents something inescapably attached.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة والقتيبي: أراد بالطائر حظه من الخير والشر من قولهم: طار سهم فلان بكذا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r1.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r1.claim: Hasan, Mujahid, and Yaqub read “and it brings forth for him,” making the bird produce the record.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r1.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد ويعقوب: " ويخرج له " بفتح الياء وضم الراء معناه: ويخرج له الطائر يوم القيامة كتابا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r2.claim: Abu Ja'far reads the verb with yāʾ, ḍamma, and fatḥa.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر " يخرج " بالياء وضمها وفتح الراء.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r3.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r3.claim: Ibn Amir and Abu Ja'far read a passive form, meaning the person is given the record.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r3.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وأبو جعفر " يلقاه " بضم الياء وفتح اللام وتشديد القاف يعني: يلقى الإنسان ذلك الكتاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r4.speaker: الباقون
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r4.claim: Other readers use the active form, meaning the person sees the record.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الياء خفيفة أي يراه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r5.claim: A report says God tells the angel to fold a person's record at death and keeps it closed until Resurrection Day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p82#2/r5.anchor: وفي الآثار: إن الله تعالى يأمر الملك بطي الصحيفة إذا تم عمر العبد فلا تنشر إلى يوم القيامة.

QASHANI:17:13-15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:17:13-15/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:17:13-15/r1.claim: Each person's fortune, good or bad, is bound to that person's nature like a collar; the author cites the saying that felicity or misery is fixed in the womb.
QASHANI:17:13-15/r1.anchor: السعيد من سعد في بطن أمه والشقي من شقى في بطن أمه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r1.claim: A person's bird is his deeds and decreed lot; bird omens become a metaphor for whatever causes good or evil, including God's decree and human action.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r1.anchor: عمله وما قدر له كأنه طير إليه من عش الغيب ووكر القدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r2.claim: Its being bound to the neck indicates the lot's unavoidable attachment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r2.anchor: فى عنقه } لزوم الطوق في عنقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r3.claim: The book on Judgment Day is either the record of one's deeds or the self imprinted by actions, since chosen acts shape the soul and repetition forms dispositions.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r3.anchor: هي صحيفة عمله أو نفسه المنتقشة بآثار أعماله

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r4.claim: The book's grammatical status can be an object or circumstantial expression from an omitted object pronoun referring to the bird; Yaqub's reading supports this, and other readings vary between forms of “bring out.”
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r4.anchor: ونصبه بأنه مفعول أو حال من مفعول محذوف

BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r5.claim: “Spread open” means the covering is removed; the terms may both describe the book, or the second may be circumstantial, and Ibn Amir reads “yalqāhu” in a passive construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:17:12-13#2/r5.anchor: لكشف الغطاء، وهما صفتان للكتاب، أو { يلقه } صفة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r1.claim: Every human is naturally restless, and the allotted bird is the person's predestined good or evil deed; the image reflects Arabs' use of omens before important actions.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r1.anchor: عمله الذي قدرناه عليه من خير وشر , ولعله عبر به لأنهم كانوا لا يقدمون ولا يحجمون

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r2.claim: The deed is bound to a person's neck, a place of adornment or disgrace, and cannot be escaped, as one cannot escape one's neck.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r2.anchor: الذي محل الزين بالقلادة ونحوها , والشين بالغل ونحوه , إلزاما لا يقدر أن ينفك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r3.claim: Israel's imposed scripture and decree likewise could not be escaped; in the end only what was eternally decreed can appear.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r3.anchor: فلا يمكن أن يظهر في الأبد إلا ما قضى به في الأزل

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r4.claim: The record contains every deed: recording angels write it daily and compare it with the Preserved Tablet, finding no discrepancy.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r4.anchor: تكتبه حفظتنا كل يوم , ثم إذا صعدوا قابلوا ما فيه على ما سطرناه قديما في اللوح المحفوظ

BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r10.claim: The passage recalls the command to inspect creation repeatedly, including the verse about sight returning humbled and weary.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p367/r10.anchor: { ثم ارجع البصر كرتين ينقلب إليك البصر خاسئا وهو حسير }

DURR-FULL:v5p248/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r7.claim: Every person's bird, understood as destiny or deeds, is attached to his neck.
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r7.anchor: عن جابر رضي الله عنه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: طائر كل إنسان في عنقه

DURR-FULL:v5p248/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r8.claim: A report describes the forming substance remaining forty days in the woman, entering her body, then being sent down to the womb as a clot.
DURR-FULL:v5p248/r8.anchor: عن حذيفة بن أسيد رضي الله عنه سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: إن النطفة التي يخلق منها النسمة تطير

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r1.speaker: الملك
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r1.claim: At four months the angel asks God about the child's bodily form, including sex, soundness, beauty, and height.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r1.anchor: فيقول: يا رب ما أصور أزائد أم ناقص أذكر أم أنثى أجميل أم ذميم

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r2.speaker: الملك
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r2.claim: The angel asks whether the child is wretched or happy; the report says that state is breathed into it at the end of its term.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r2.anchor: ثم يقول الملك: يا رب أشقي أم سعيد فإن كان سعيدا نفخ فيه بالسعادة

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r3.speaker: الملك
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r3.claim: The angel is told to record the person's effects, provision, affliction, and obedient or sinful deeds as God commands.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r3.anchor: ثم يقول: اكتب أثرها ورزقها ومصيبتها وعملها بالطاعة والمعصية فيكتب من ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r4.speaker: الله
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r4.claim: The written decree is hung around the person's neck until God's judgment concerning him.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r4.anchor: فيقول: علقه في عنقه إلى قضائي عليه فذلك قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه}

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r5.claim: The attached bird is a person's happiness or misery and everything decreed for or against him, following him wherever he goes.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r5.anchor:
عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في
قوله: {ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} قال: سعادته وشقاوته وما قدره الله له

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r6.speaker: عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r6.claim: The bird means a person's misery or happiness, provision, and lifespan.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r6.anchor: قال: قال عبد الله رضي الله عنه الشقاء والسعادة والرزق والأجل

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r7.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r7.claim: Anas explains the bird attached to the neck as the person's book or record.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r7.anchor: عن أنس رضي الله عنه في قوله: {طائره في عنقه} قال: كتابه

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r8.claim: The bird attached to a person means his own deeds.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} أي عمله

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r9.claim: Every newborn has a leaf around its neck recording whether the child is wretched or happy.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} قال: ما من مولود يولد

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r10.claim: The bird is one's deeds; the published book is the counted record of what one did, presented to be read at resurrection.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: {ألزمناه طائره} قال: عمله {ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا}

DURR-FULL:v5p249/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r11.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r11.claim: An unbeliever sees his book and asks God to let him audit himself, acknowledging that God does not wrong His servants.
DURR-FULL:v5p249/r11.anchor: عن السدي رضي الله عنه في الآية قال: الكافر يخرج له يوم القيامة كتاب فيقول: رب إنك قد قضيت

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.claim: After the unbeliever asks to judge himself, he is told to read his book, which suffices as his reckoner.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r1.anchor: فيقال له: {اقرأ كتابك كفى بنفسك اليوم عليك حسيبا}

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r2.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy has each person read his attached bird on resurrection as a published book.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r2.anchor: عن هرون قال: في قراءة أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} يقرؤه يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r3.claim: Mujahid reads the verb with an open ya, understanding that the bird itself is brought out as a book.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ ويخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا بفتح الياء يعني يخرج الطائر كتابا

DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.claim: Two noble angels write each person's record; at death it is rolled and placed around the person's neck in the grave until resurrection, when the person reads it.
DURR-FULL:v5p250/r5.anchor: عن الحسن رضي الله عنه قال: يا ابن آدم بسطت لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان كريمان أحدهما عن يمينك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.claim: After encouragement and warning, the passage highlights God’s exhaustive knowledge of deeds, comparing their precise accounting to written records; the specific human deeds follow the general “everything” for emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r1.anchor: فأعقب ذكر ما فصله الله من الأشياء بالتنبيه على تفصيل أعمال الناس تفصيلا لا يقبل الشك ولا الإخفاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r2.claim: Every person’s allotted “bird” is the deed God has already determined in His knowledge, which the person inevitably performs in worldly life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r2.anchor: قدرنا له عمله في علمنا فهو عامل به لا محالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r3.claim: Ṭā’ir can mean an arrow, lot, or marked slip assigning a person a share in a distribution; reports use it for the share allotted by lot.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r3.anchor: أطلق على السهم ، أو القرطاس الذي يعين فيه صاحب الحظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r4.claim: The allotment metaphor may come from drawing named arrows, whose feathering let them pierce the air when shot at divided shares.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r4.anchor: كانوا يرمون السهام المرقومة بأسماء المتقاسمين على صبر الشيء المقسوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, it derives from bird omens used especially on journeys; the bird’s sign came to mean a person’s fortune for good or ill.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p46#2/r5.anchor: من زجر الطير لمعرفة بختت أو شؤم الزاجر من حالة الطير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r1.claim: Ilzām means making something inseparable, as in the ordinary use of لزمه.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r1.anchor: جعله لازما له ، أي غير مفارق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r2.claim: “In his neck” may picture the deed’s closeness as a necklace, since necklaces are worn around the neck.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون كناية عن الملازمة والقرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r3.speaker: الأعشى
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r3.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s verse uses the verb “I put a necklace on it,” illustrating the necklace image.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r4.claim: The phrase may reflect a known practice of hanging marks around people’s necks to designate their duties or status, including a mark used for protected non-Muslims.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r4.anchor: تمثيلا لحالة لعلها كانت معروفة عند العرب وهي وضع علامات تعلق في الرقاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r5.speaker: بشار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r5.claim: Bashshar’s poem says love was inscribed on his neck like the signet of a protected person, exemplifying neck-marking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r5.anchor: كتب الحب لها في عنقي موضع الخاتم من أهله الذمم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r6.claim: A third image is a camel marked on the neck or fitted with a bell so it can be identified and not lost.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r6.anchor: تمثيلا بالبعير الذي يوسم في عنقه بسمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r7.claim: All these images mean that a person receives the full consequence of their good or evil deeds; this differs from the written book described next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r7.anchor: والمعنى على الجميع أن كل إنسان يعامل بعمله من خير أو شر لا ينقص له منه شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r8.claim: The following statement says those deeds will be visibly itemized at resurrection, with nothing small or great omitted from recompense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r8.anchor: تظهر يوم القيامة مفصلة معينة لا تغادر منها صغيرة ولا كبيرة إلا أحصيت للجزاء عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r9.claim: Most readers read ونخرج with the majestic first-person plural and a kasra on rā’; Yaʿqub instead reads the third-person verb referring to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { ونخرج } بنون العظمة وبكسر الراء ، وقرأه يعقوب بياء الغيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the verb passively with third-person yā’; له is the subject and كتابا its object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r10.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر بياء الغيبة في أوله مبنيا للنائب على أن { له } نائب فاعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r11.claim: The book records and counts deeds; spreading it is the opposite of folding, and يلقاه means “finds it,” conveying its ready availability.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r11.anchor: والكتاب : ما فيه ذكر الأعمال وإحصاؤها . والنشر : ضد الطي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r12.claim: The open book suggests the person can immediately inspect everything he did, as it arrives already opened for reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p47/r12.anchor: والنشر كناية عن سرعة اطلاعه على جميع ما عمله بحيث إن الكتاب يحضر من قبل وصول صاحبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r1.speaker: ابن عامر، أبو جعفر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Abu Jaʿfar read يُلَقَّاه with passive intensive form, meaning the person is made to receive or encounter the book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر ، وأبو جعفر { يلقاه بضم الياء وتشديد ، القاف مبنيا للمجهول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p48/r2.claim: Unfolding the book means displaying it to be read, as in the verse about the pages being spread.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ, and Mujāhid read ṭayra instead of ṭāʾirahu.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r10.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء ومجاهد «طيره في عنقه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says one's bird is what has been decreed for or against that person; the image addresses Arab omen customs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس طائره ما قدر له وعليه، وخاطب الله العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r12.claim: The verse rejects omen-belief: each person's good and evil are decreed and their deeds and acquisitions bound to them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r12.anchor: جميع ما يلقى الإنسان من خير وشر قد سبق به القضاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r13.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r13.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet saying, “There is no contagion and no ill omen.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442/r13.anchor: وروى جابر بن عبد الله أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا عدوى ولا طيرة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r1.claim: Bird imagery stands for one's attached lot and deeds; Mujāhid and Qatāda connect it with Arab expressions for luck.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r1.anchor: فعبر عن الحظ والعمل إذ هما متلازمان ب «الطائر» ، قال مجاهد وقتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r2.speaker: أم العلاء الأنصارية
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r2.claim: Umm al-ʿAlāʾ says that among the emigrants allotted to them was ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn; “what flew to us” means their share.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r2.anchor: كقول أم العلا الأنصارية فطار لنا من القادمين مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r3.claim: The neck conventionally represents an obligation, collar, or trust; al-Aʿshā's poem is an example.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r3.anchor: في عنقه جرى أيضا على مقطع العرب في أن تنسب ما كان إلزاما وقلادة وأمانة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r4.claim: Earning, injury, and sin are assigned to the hand because it is the chief means of acquisition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r4.anchor: ما كان تكسبا وجناية وإثما منسوبا إلى اليد إذ هي الأصل في التكسب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r5.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Nāfiʿ, and common readers read “We bring out” with first-person plural and kitāban accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ونافع والناس «ونخرج» بنون العظمة «كتابا» بالنصب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, and Ibn Muḥayṣin read yukhraju with kitāban as object; al-Ḥasan also transmits nominative kitāb.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r6.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن: و «يخرج» بفتح الياء وضم الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r7.claim: Other readings attributed to Abū Jaʿfar include passive yuḵraju; Ubayy's codex adds “he reads it on Resurrection.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r7.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «في عنقه يقرؤه يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r8.claim: The record is the person's deeds and sins.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r8.anchor: وهذا الكتاب هو عمل الإنسان وخطيئاته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r9.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r9.claim: Most read yalaqāhu with light qāf; Ibn ʿĀmir reads it with doubled qāf.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «يلقاه» بفتح الياء وسكون اللام وخفة القاف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes two recording angels; the record is folded at death, follows the person through the grave, and opens at resurrection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p442#2/r11.anchor: أسند الطبري عن الحسن أنه قال: يا ابن آدم بسطت لك صحيفتك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r1.claim: On al-Ḥasan's account, the “bird” is the person's collected deeds accompanying him in the grave; Ibn ʿAbbās is said to hold this.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p443/r1.anchor: يكون الطائر ما يتحصل مع آدم من عمله في قبره

SULAMI:v1p383#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p383#2/r3.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p383#2/r3.claim: Al-Nasrabadi contrasts states people impose on themselves with states imposed by God, whose demands are harder; some must patiently sustain witnessing, while others must keep the etiquette of nearness.
SULAMI:v1p383#2/r3.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : ألزمت نفسك أحوالا وألزمت أحوالا ، وما ألزمته أشد مما ألزمته نفسك

SULAMI:v1p384#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r1.claim: Some distinguish two books: one written by a person through the days and hours, and another written for that person in pre-eternity; neither is the other.
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : كتابا : تكتبه على نفسك في أيامك وساعاتك . وكتاب كتب عليك في الأزل

SULAMI:v1p384#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r2.claim: Some say the book is composed from one's speech, saliva, limbs, and joints; the person dictated it to the recording angels, and the self becomes its witness when anything is denied.
SULAMI:v1p384#2/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : الكتاب الذي يخرج إليك هو كتاب لسانك قلمه ، وريقك مداده ، وأعضاؤك ومفاصلك قرطاسه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r1.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r1.claim: He reads kullu with the lām nominative rather than accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة وكل برفع اللام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي والحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r2.claim: They read ṭāʾir as ṭayri, with yāʾ and without alif.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي والحسن ألزمناه طيره بياء ساكنة من غير الف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r3.claim: One view identifies a person's allotted bird with their misery or felicity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r3.anchor: شقاوته وسعادته قاله أبو صالح عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r4.claim: Mujahid says every newborn has a leaf around its neck marked either wretched or happy.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة مكتوب فيها شقي أو سعيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that the bird signifies a person's deeds; al-Hasan is also reported to hold both this and the preceding view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r5.anchor: عمله قاله الفراء وعن الحسن كالقولين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r6.speaker: خصيف
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r6.claim: A further view takes the bird as whatever befalls a person; Abu Ubayda glosses it as one's allotted share.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r6.anchor: انه ما يصيبه قاله خصيف وقال أبو عبيدة حظه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains it as each person's divinely allotted share of good and evil, which remains bound to that person; bird language echoes Arab omens.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r7.anchor: لكل امرئ حظا من الخير والشر قد قضاه الله عليه فهو لازم عنقه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r8.claim: The Qur'an addresses Arabs in their own omen idiom, teaching that what they assign to a bird is actually attached to their own necks.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r8.anchor: فخاطبهم الله بما يستعملون واعلمهم ان ذلك الأمر الذي يجعلونه بالطائر هو الذي يلزمه أعناقهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r9.speaker: الأزهري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r9.claim: God knew and recorded Adam's obedient and disobedient descendants, decreeing felicity for the first and misery for the second; each person's destiny is fixed at creation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r9.anchor: علم المطيع من ذريته والعاصي فكتب ما علمه منهم اجمعين وقضى سعادة من علمه مطيعا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r10.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r10.claim: The bird can mean the person's deeds from which people themselves would take omens; neck signifies that the deeds remain attached to them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r10.anchor: ما يتطير من مثله من شيء عمله وذكر العنق عبارة عن اللزوم له

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r11.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r11.claim: The Arabs called deeds birds because they used to take omens from certain actions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r11.anchor: الاصل في تسميتهم العمل طائرا انهم كانوا يتطيرون من بعض الاعمال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r12.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r12.claim: He reads the passive verb yukhraju with yāʾ, ḍamma, and fatḥ on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r12.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويخرج بياء مضمومة وفتح الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r13.speaker: يعقوب وعبد الوارث
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r13.claim: They read yukhraju with open yāʾ and ḍamma on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r13.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب وعبد الوارث بالياء مفتوحة وضم الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r14.speaker: قتادة وأبو المتوكل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r14.claim: They read yukhraju with nominative yāʾ and kasra on the rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r14.anchor: وقرأ قتادة وابو المتوكل ويخرج بياء مرفوعة وكسر الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r15.speaker: أبو الجوزاء والأعرج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r15.claim: They read the verb with an open tāʾ and nominative rāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r15.anchor: وقرأ أبو الجوزاء والأعرج وتخرج بتاء مفتوحة ورفع الراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r16.speaker: ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r16.claim: They read kitāb in the nominative rather than accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r16.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وعكرمة والضحاك كتاب بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r17.speaker: ابن عامر وأبو جعفر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r17.claim: They read yulaqqāhu with ḍamma on the yāʾ and a doubled qāf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r17.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وابو جعفر يلقاه بضم الياء وتشديد القاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r18.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r18.claim: They incline the qāf in yulaqqāhu.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r19.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r19.claim: The book is the record of a person's deeds.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r19.anchor: قال المفسرون هذا كتابه الذي فيه ما عمل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r20.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r20.speaker: أبو السوار العدوي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r20.claim: He likens the record to an open page during life, folded at death, and opened again at resurrection, urging people to write what they wish while alive.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p15/r20.anchor: فصحيفتك منشورة فأمل فيها ما شئت فاذا مت طويت ثم اذا بعثت نشرت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and other early interpreters explain a person's “bird” as all his good and bad deeds, which remain attached to him for recompense.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r1.anchor: وطائره: هو ما طار عنه من عمله، كما قال ابن عباس ومجاهد وغير واحد: من خير وشر،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.claim: Every deed, small or great, is preserved and written down day and night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r2.anchor: والمقصود أن عمل ابن آدم محفوظ عليه، قليله وكثيره، ويكتب عليه ليلا ونهارا، صباحا ومساء.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r3.claim: A report from Jabir has the Prophet say each person's bird is tied to his neck; Ibn Luhay'a glosses “bird” as augury, which Ibn Kathir calls very strange.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.claim: The neck is singled out because it is a distinctive body part; something fastened there cannot be escaped.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p50#2/r6.anchor: إنما ذكر العنق؛ لأنه عضو لا نظير له في (5) الجسد، ومن ألزم بشيء فيه فلا محيد له عنه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r1.speaker: الشاعر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r1.claim: An unattributed poetic line about carrying something as a dove's collar illustrates the image of a deed fastened to the neck.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r1.anchor: اذهب بها اذهب بها … طوقتها طوق الحمامة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r2.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet saying there is no contagion or augury and every person has his bird attached to his neck.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r2.anchor: لا عدوى ولا طيرة وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r3.speaker: جابر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r3.claim: A connected report from Jabir has the Prophet say each servant's bird is at his neck.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r4.speaker: عقبة بن عامر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r4.claim: The Prophet says each day's deeds are sealed; when a believer is ill, God orders the angels to record his usual deeds until he recovers or dies. Ibn Kathir grades the chain good and strong.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p51/r4.anchor: ليس من عمل يوم إلا وهو يختم عليه، فإذا مرض المؤمن قالت الملائكة

TUSTARI:17:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:17:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:17:13/r1.claim: The ‘bird’ assigned to each person is his knowledge of what he has done, whether good or evil.
TUSTARI:17:13/r1.anchor: قال: علمه أي ما كان من خير وشر.

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r1.claim: Night and day indicate a wise governor and a great blessing.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r1.anchor: ويدل الليل والنهار على مدبر حكيم ونعمة عظيمة مما يطول تفصيلها

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads passively: the person's allotted bird, understood as his deed, produces a book.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r2.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر يخرج بضم الياء وفتح الراء على ما لم يسم فاعله

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r3.speaker: يعقوب، والحسن، ومجاهد
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r3.claim: They read with the deed as agent: the person's deed is brought out as a book.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r3.anchor: قرأ يعقوب، والحسن، ومجاهد: يخرج بفتح الياء وبضم الراء

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r4.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r4.claim: An alternative parsing says the bird is brought out and becomes a book.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r4.anchor: وقيل: تقديره: يخرج له الطائر فيصير كتابا

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r5.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r5.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads the verb as God bringing out the book; it can also mean the bird emerges.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r5.anchor: قرأ يحيى بن وثاب: ويخرج بضم الياء وكسر الراء على تقدير:

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r6.speaker: القراء
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r6.claim: The other readers use “We bring out”; Abu ʿAmr supports the first-person plural by the preceding “We bound.”
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r6.anchor: والقراء على: ونخرج بالنون وضمها وكسر الراء على معنى:

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r7.claim: Abu ʿAmr supports this reading by its continuity with “We bound.”
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r7.anchor: واحتج أبو عمرو لهذه القراءة بقوله: ألزمناه.

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r8.claim: They read the book as handed to the person; the remaining readers read that the person sees it.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر: كتابا يلقاه بضم الياء وفتح اللام

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r9.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء العطاردي
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r9.claim: They read ṭayr without alif; the meaning is the same as ṭāʾir.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r9.anchor: وعن الحسن ومجاهد وأبي رجاء العطاردي: طيره بغير ألف والمعنى واحد.

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r10.claim: Of two definitions of the human, the author prefers the first: an animal in human form.

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r11.claim: A person's ṭāʾir is his deed; the word also means an omen or allotment.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r11.anchor: وطائر الإنسان عمله، والطير التطير من الشيء،

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r12.claim: The expression derives from Arab bird-omens, based on auspicious or inauspicious birds in flight.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r12.anchor: عبر عنه بالطائر على عادة العرب فيما كانت تتفاءل أو تتشاءم به

JISHUMI:v6p4169/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r13.claim: A report uses “I allotted the garment among my wives” for distributing shares.
JISHUMI:v6p4169/r13.anchor: ومنه الحديث: فأطرت الحلة في نسائي أي: قسمتها،

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r1.claim: Deeds remain attached to each person, exhorting obedience and warning against disobedience.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r1.anchor: يدل أول الآيات أن جزاء أعمالهم لازم لهم،

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says two angels record good and bad deeds; the scroll is folded around the person after death until resurrection.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن أن عليه موكلان يكتبان خيره وشره،

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r3.claim: Knowing that deeds are recorded benefits the morally responsible person.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r3.anchor: وفي علم المكلف به لطف له.

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r14.claim: Against determinism, “his bird” means the person's deed, attributing it to him rather than solely to its alleged divine creator.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r14.anchor: منها: قوله: طائره أي: عمله فكيف ألزمه وأضافه إليه،

JISHUMI:v6p4173/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r15.claim: If God created deeds, the author asks why a person's deeds are written against him.
JISHUMI:v6p4173/r15.anchor: ومنها: قوله: (ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا) وهو ما يكتب عليه،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r1.claim: Ṭāʾir means a person's deed; Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna alternatively connects it to an arrow drawn in a lot, meaning the deed assigned to that person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r1.anchor: طئره } عمله وقد حققنا القول فيه في سورة النمل . وعن ابن عيينة : هو من قولك : طار له سهم ، إذا خرج

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r2.claim: A person's deed clings to him like a necklace or shackle and cannot be removed, as in Arab proverbs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r2.anchor: والمعنى أن عمله لازم له لزوم القلادة أو الغل لا يفك عنه ، ومنه مثل العرب : تقلدها طوق الحمامة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r3.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says each person's record is spread out and placed around his neck at resurrection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r3.anchor: عن الحسن : يا ابن آدم بسطت لك صحيفة إذا بعثت قلدتها في عنقك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r4.claim: Readings include a quiescent nūn in his neck; nukh riju with nūn; yukhraju with God as subject or passive; and yakhruju with the deed as subject producing a record.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r4.anchor: وقرىء : ( في عنقه ) بسكون النون . وقرىء : ( نخرج ) بالنون . ( ويخرج ) بالياء ، والضمير لله عز وجل ( ويخرج ) ، على البناء للمفعول

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r5.claim: On the reading where the deed itself comes out, book is a circumstantial accusative; yalaqāhu is also read doubled and passive.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p610/r5.anchor: ويخرج من خرج ، والضمير للطائر . أي : يخرج الطائر كتابا ، وانتصاب { كتابا } على الحال . وقرىء : ( يلقاه ) ، بالتشديد مبنيا للمفعول

FARRA:v2p117/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p117/r6.claim: A person’s طائر is his deed, good or bad.
FARRA:v2p117/r6.anchor: وقوله: وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره [13] وهو عمله، إن خيرا فخيرا وإن شرا فشرا

FARRA:v2p117/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r7.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
FARRA:v2p117/r7.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read ونخرج له with nūn; others read ويخرج له with a fatḥa on yāʾ, including Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan.
FARRA:v2p117/r7.anchor: قرأها يحيى بن وثاب بالنون وقرأها غيره بالياء مفتوحة

FARRA:v2p117/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p117/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر المدني
FARRA:v2p117/r8.claim: Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read ويخرج له كتابا, meaning the person’s deed is brought out as a book; all readings are acceptable.
FARRA:v2p117/r8.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر المدني (ويخرج ... له كتابا) معناه: ويخرج له عمله كتابا.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r1.claim: One reading of each person's طائر is his good or bad deeds, likened to Arab omens from birds passing on the right or left.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r1.anchor: ألزمناه عمله من خير أو شر مثل ما كانت العرب تقوله

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r2.claim: Alternatively, طائره means a person's allotted fortune or share, as in the Arab expression for a سهم that falls to someone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r2.anchor: من قول العرب : طار سهم فلان إذا خرج سهمه ونصيبه منه , قاله أبو عبيدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r3.claim: The opened record is the record of the person's good or bad deeds represented by his طائر.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r3.anchor: يعني كتاب طائره الذي في عنقه من خير أو شر

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r4.claim: The record may be spread out to hasten good news for good deeds and rebuke for bad ones.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r4.anchor: أحدهما : تعجيلا للبشرى بالحسنة , والتوبيخ بالسيئة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r5.claim: Alternatively, its being spread out publicly displays the person's deeds, good or bad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p233/r5.anchor: إظهار عمله من خير أو شر

MUJAHID:v1p359/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
MUJAHID:v1p359/r1.claim: A person's bird fastened to his neck is his deed, good and bad.
MUJAHID:v1p359/r1.anchor: ﴿ ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ﴾ قال عمله خيره وشره

MUJAHID:v1p359/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p359/r2.speaker: الحسن
MUJAHID:v1p359/r2.claim: Hasan explains the person's deed as encompassing good and bad, misery and felicity.
MUJAHID:v1p359/r2.anchor: عن الحسن قال ﴿ طائره ﴾ عمله خيره وشره شقاوته وسعادته

MUQATIL:17:13-14/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r1.claim: Each person's deed, good or bad, is fastened to the neck and stays with that person until the reckoning; on Resurrection Day the deed-record is opened and handed over.
MUQATIL:17:13-14/r1.anchor: يعني عمله الذي عمل، خيرا كان أو شرا، فهو { في عنقه } لا يفارقه حتى يحاسب عليه، { ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا }

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets ṭāʾir as a person’s allotted share.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: حظه. وقال المفسرون:

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r2.speaker: المفسرون
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r2.claim: The commentators say ṭāʾir is the good or evil deed fastened around a person’s neck.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r2.anchor: وقال المفسرون: ما عمل من خير أو شر ألزمناه عنقه (2) .

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r3.claim: He says both earlier explanations need clarification.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r4.claim: He prefers that each person has a divinely decreed share of good and evil that remains bound to the person.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r4.anchor: والمعنى فيما أرى- والله أعلم -: أن لكل امرئ حظا من الخير والشر قد قضاه الله عليه. فهو لازم عنقه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r5.claim: Arabic calls anything that remains attached to a person something bound to the neck, as in saying a debt is in one’s neck until discharged.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r5.anchor: والعرب تقول لكل ما لزم الإنسان: قد لزم عنقه. وهو لازم صليف عنقه (3) . وهذا لك علي وفي عنقي حتى أخرج منه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r6.claim: The share is called ṭāʾir because Arabs describe good or evil as a bird that has flown to someone, using an omen’s cause for its result; God speaks in their idiom and locates that fate with them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r6.anchor: وإنما قيل للحظ من الخير والشر: طائر؛ لقول العرب: جرى له الطائر بكذا من الخير، وجرى له الطائر بكذا من الشر؛

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu Raja, and Mujahid recite ṭayrih without the alif; the two readings mean the same, since ṭayr can denote a group and ṭāʾir one bird.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#2/r7.anchor: وكان الحسن وأبو رجاء ومجاهد يقرؤون: (وكل إنسان ألزمناه طيره في عنقه) بلا ألف. والمعنيان جميعا سواء؛

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#3/r1.claim: In the reading with nukh'riju, God brings the person’s deed out as a book; with yukh'raju, that deed itself brings the book out.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p252#3/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا} أي نخرج بذلك العمل كتابا. ومن قرأ "ويخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا" أراد: ويخرج ذلك العمل كتابا.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r1.claim: A person's ṭāʾir is his deeds, which cling to him like a necklace or shackle that cannot be removed.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r1.anchor: يعنى أن عمله لازم له لزوم القلادة أو الغل للعنق

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r2.speaker: الشامي
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r2.claim: Al-Shāmī reads “a book that he will meet,” with the clause describing the book.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r3.claim: The book is spread out when the person meets it, so it is not folded and can be read; alternatively, both clauses describe the book.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r3.anchor: حال من يلقاه يعنى غير مطوى ليمكنه قراءته أو هما صفتان للكتاب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.claim: The narration continues that God will say to the person to read the book.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p281/r4.anchor: حال من يلقاه يعنى غير مطوى ليمكنه قراءته

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r1.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the neck image expresses how tightly a person’s allotted fate clings, as a necklace clings to the neck.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: ذكر العنق عبارة عن اللزوم كلزوم القلادة للعنق.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the person’s bird as the deeds and the good and evil decreed for them, which accompany them wherever they go.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «طائره» عمله وما قدر عليه من خير وشر، وهو ملازمه أينما كان.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r3.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r3.claim: They say a person’s good and evil remain with them until they are called to account.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل والكلبي: خيره وشره معه لا يفارقه حتى يحاسب به.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r4.claim: Mujahid explains the bird as a person’s work and livelihood; another report from him says each newborn has a note recording blessedness or wretchedness.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عمله ورزقه، وعنه: ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r5.claim: Hasan reads the bird as a person’s destined happiness or misery and the good or evil allotted in eternity.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن: «ألزمناه طائره» أي شقاوته وسعادته وما كتب له من خير وشر

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r6.claim: Another interpretation is that the image means the duty to follow religious law, which a person is capable of obeying or violating.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r6.anchor: وقيل: أراد به التكليف، أي قدرناه التزام الشرع

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r7.claim: The spread-out book on Judgment Day is the written record represented by the bird fastened to a person’s neck.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r7.anchor: يعني كتاب طائره الذي في عنقه.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r8.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r8.claim: They read طيره without the alif, a form also reflected in the reported supplication denying any omen apart from God’s decree.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r8.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء ومجاهد: «طيره» بغير ألف

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r9.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن وأبو جعفر ويعقوب
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r9.claim: They read ويُخرج in the active form; the bird may bring out the book or itself become a book.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن وأبو جعفر ويعقوب «ويخرج» بفتح الياء وضم الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r10.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r10.claim: Mujahid is also reported to read the form as God bringing out the book.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r10.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب «ويخرج» بضم الياء وكسر الراء وروي عن مجاهد أي يخرج الله

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r11.speaker: شيبة ومحمد بن السميقع وأبو جعفر
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r11.claim: They read the verb passively, meaning that the bird is brought out as a book for the person.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r11.anchor: وقرأ شيبة ومحمد بن السميقع، وروي أيضا عن أبي جعفر: «ويخرج» بضم الياء وفتح الراء

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r12.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r12.claim: The majority reading says “We bring out”; Abu Amr supports it by its parallel with “We fastened it to him.”
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r12.anchor: الباقون «ونخرج» بنون مضمومة وكسر الراء أي ونحن نخرج. احتج أبو عمرو

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر والحسن وابن عامر
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r13.claim: They read يُلَقَّاه, meaning that the person is given the book; the majority read يَلْقَاه, meaning that they see it spread open.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر والحسن وابن عامر «يلقاه» بضم الياء وفتح اللام وتشديد القاف

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r14.claim: The word “spread open” hastens the announcement of good news for good deeds and reproach for evil deeds.

QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r15.speaker: أبو السوار العدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r15.claim: He describes two stages of the record: it remains open during life, then is folded at death and reopened at resurrection.
QURTUBI-FULL:17:13-14/r15.anchor: قال: هما نشرتان وطية أما ما حييت يابن آدم فصحيفتك المنشورة

MAJAZ:v1p370/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p370/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p370/r8.claim: طائره means a person’s allotted share or fortune.

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.claim: The passage follows the completed explanation of signs and warning: because revelation has removed excuses, each person will face a record and answer for deeds.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r1.anchor: كل ما يحتاج إليه من دلائل التوحيد والنبوة والمعاد فقد صار مذكورا

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.claim: A second link is that God’s provision of worldly and religious benefits entails that people should serve and obey Him, so their deeds are questioned.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r2.anchor: وذلك يقتضي وجوب اشتغالهم بخدمته وطاعته

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.claim: A third link is that creation is for worship; the sun, moon, night, and day enable obedience, which is then assessed at resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r3.anchor: فلما شرح أحوال الشمس والقمر والليل والنهار

RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r4.claim: Arab omen-taking from birds’ direction and manner of flight led “bird/omen” to signify a person’s good or evil deeds; this is supported by the reading of Hasan and Mujahid.
RAZI-FULL:v20p133#2/r4.anchor: قراءة الحسن ومجاهد : { ألزمناه طئره فى عنقه }

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r1.claim: Abu Ubayda says “bird” means a person’s lot or fortune, called bakht in Persian.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r1.anchor: الطائر عند العرب الحظ وهو الذي تسميه الفرس البخت

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r2.claim: Razi explains the assigned “bird” as each person’s decreed share of intellect, lifespan, provision, and felicity or misery, which inevitably reaches them.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r2.anchor: كل ما قدره الله تعالى ومضى في علمه حصوله ، فهو لازم له

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r3.claim: The binding of the assigned deed supports the claim that whatever God decrees in prior knowledge must occur and cannot fail to occur.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r3.anchor: كل ما قدره الله تعالى للإنسان وحكم عليه به في سابق علمه

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r4.claim: He argues first that an assigned deed is necessarily obtained because what is made binding cannot be removed.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r4.anchor: وما كان لازما للشيء كان ممتنع الزوال عنه واجب الحصول له

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r5.claim: He argues second that God explicitly attributes the binding to Himself, comparing it with binding people to piety.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r5.anchor: وهذه الآية دالة على أنه لا يظهر في الأبد إلا ما حكم الله به

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying that the Pen has dried concerning what will occur until Resurrection reinforces the decree argument; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r6.anchor: جف القلم بما هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r7.claim: “On his neck” is an idiom for an obligation assigned to someone, like placing a task or responsibility in one’s neck as a collar.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r7.anchor: كناية عن اللزوم كما يقال : جعلت هذا في عنقك

RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r8.claim: The neck is singled out because good deeds adorn their bearer like jewelry, while sins disgrace and shackle like a collar.
RAZI-FULL:v20p134/r8.anchor: وإنما خص العنق من بين سائر الأعضاء بهذا المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r1.claim: Hasan says two recording angels preserve good deeds on the right and sins on the left; after death the record is folded and kept with the person until it is brought out at Resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r1.anchor: يا ابن آدم بسطنا لك صحيفة ووكل بك ملكان فهما عن يمينك وشمالك

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r2.claim: “We bring it out for him” can mean bringing the hidden record from the grave when the person is raised.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r2.anchor: يجوز أن يكون معناه : نخرج له ذلك لأنه لم ير كتابه في الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r3.speaker: يعقوب
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r3.claim: Yaqub reads the verb in the passive, understood as the person’s deed or “bird” being brought out as an opened book.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r3.anchor: أي يخرج له الطائر أي عمله كتابا منشورا

RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r4.claim: Ibn Umar reads “he meets it” as “he is handed it,” by analogy with language for presenting something to someone.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135/r4.anchor: من قولهم : لقيت فلانا الشيء أي استقبلته به

RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r1.claim: A person’s deeds resemble birds flying toward them because God’s eternal decree of good and evil must reach each person; recognizing this shows the need for eternal divine care.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r1.anchor: قدر لكل أحد في الأزل مقدارا من الخير والشر

RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r2.claim: Every event is preceded by another event in a chain established by God, like countless birds launched from pre-eternity toward a particular person, time, and condition.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r2.anchor: جعل لكل حادث حادثا متقدما عليه لحصول الحادث المتأخر

RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.claim: Repeated voluntary acts form stable habits in the soul; each act leaves an effect, as repeated water drops eventually bore a stone.
RAZI-FULL:v20p135#2/r3.anchor: تكرار الأعمال الاختيارية تفيد حدوث الملكة النفسانية الراسخة في جوهر النفس

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.claim: Every deed leaves a trace in the soul: attraction from creation toward God brings felicity, while attraction away from God toward created things brings misery.
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r1.anchor: كل عمل يصدر من الإنسان كثيرا كان أو قليلا قويا كان أو ضعيفا

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r2.claim: The body’s governance hides these traces; when its bond ends at death, the soul rises and the Resurrection begins in this spiritual sense.

RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.claim: The opened book is the soul’s previously hidden worldly impressions, now exposed after bodily attachment ends and read by the intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v20p136/r3.anchor: ونخرج له عند حصول هذه القيامة من عمق البدن المظلم كتابا مشتملا على جميع تلك الآثار

RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.claim: Razi affirms the apparent narrated events as true while allowing the spiritual interpretations; he calls affirming both the sound, straight approach.
RAZI-FULL:v20p137/r1.anchor: الأحوال الظاهرة التي وردت فيها الروايات حق وصدق لا مرية فيها

NAHHAS:v2p417/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p417/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p417/r21.claim: كل إنسان is likewise accusative with an implicit verb; منشورا describes the book as an adjective or circumstantial state.
NAHHAS:v2p417/r21.anchor: من نعت كتاب ، وان شئت على الحال

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r1.claim: Ṭāʾirah (“omen”) derives from the root for birds because early Arabs and other premodern societies treated birds’ behavior as signs of fortune or consequences.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r1.anchor: since the early Arabs, like certain other premodern societies, considered the movement and behavior of birds

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r2.claim: The omen fastened on the neck depicts foreknown destiny as sealed; the neck also bears tokens of honor or shame such as necklaces, chains, and collars.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r2.anchor: That God has fastened a human being’s omen upon his neck is an image used to convey the idea that God has foreknowledge of a human being’s ultimate destiny

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r3.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r3.claim: Many commentators identify the omen with a person’s deeds, which portend bliss or misery in the Hereafter, and also with that individual’s Divine Decree (qadar).
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r3.anchor: Many commentators consider the omen upon one’s neck to represent one’s deeds in life, which, like an omen, portend either bliss or wretchedness

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r4.claim: Traditions say each person is divinely apportioned a lifespan, provision, offspring, and status in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r4.anchor: all human beings are born with a Divinely apportioned life span, material provision, and number of offspring

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r5.claim: The verse and traditions can support predestination, but can instead indicate God’s foreknowledge of eventual moral choices and fate; some read the omen as moral responsibility (taklīf) under divine law.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r5.anchor: Both these traditions and the present verse can be read in a predestinarian vein to indicate that all moral destiny is foreordained

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.claim: The open book is the record of one’s deeds, familiar to the person and God; hidden earthly deeds and consequences become manifest in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r6.anchor: That an individual’s book is wide open indicates that its contents are well known to the individual as well as to God

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.claim: Many commentators say two angels assigned to each person record good and evil deeds.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r7.anchor: The recording of deeds is often ascribed to two angels assigned to every individual, one recording good deeds and the other evil deeds

STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.speaker: al-Rāzī
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī metaphorically pictures each deed as a drop leaving an impression on the soul’s rock; repeated habits help inscribe a person’s destiny.
STUDYQURAN:17:13/r8.anchor: Al-Rāzī, however, describes the spiritual reality of this recording metaphorically, suggesting that every deed one commits in life is like a drop of water

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r1.claim: The person's bird is the destiny God attaches permanently to the person: the deeds and resulting misery or happiness decreed for them; the metaphor invokes Arabs' omens from birds' directions.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r1.anchor: فأعلمهم جل ثناؤه أن كل إنسان منهم قد ألزمه ربه طائره في عنقه نحسا كان ذلك الذي ألزمه من الطائر،

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet rejects contagion and bird omens, then says each person has their bird attached to them.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، عن جابر بن عبد الله، أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «لا عدوى ولا طيرة وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه»

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the bird is one's deed, though bird language can also refer to the omens people take from one another.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} [الإسراء: 13] قال: الطائر: عمله،

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī, says one's deeds and decreed portion stay with the person wherever they go.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: أخبرني عطاء الخراساني عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} [الإسراء: 13] قال: عمله وما قدر عليه،

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r5.claim: Mujāhid identifies the bird as one's deeds and what God has written for them.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r5.anchor: قال: ابن جريج: وأخبرني عبد الله بن كثير، عن مجاهد، قال: عمله وما كتب الله له

TAB-FULL:v14p519/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r6.claim: Mujāhid also says every newborn has a written paper around the neck declaring them blessed or wretched, recording what was decreed for them.
TAB-FULL:v14p519/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} [الإسراء: 13] قال: ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة مكتوب فيها شقي أو سعيد.

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r1.claim: Qatāda says a person's bird is their deeds and the happiness or misery those deeds bring.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} [الإسراء: 13] إي والله بسعادته وشقائه بعمله

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r2.claim: The neck is used because it bears marks, necklaces, and adornments or signs of shame; Arabic therefore places binding traits there, just as it attributes deeds to the hand regardless of which limb performed them.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r2.anchor: لأن العنق هو موضع السمات، وموضع القلائد والأطوقة، وغير ذلك مما يزين أو يشين،

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r3.claim: Most Medinan, Meccan, and Iraqi readers read wa-nukhriju with the divine plural and yalqāhu with an active yāʾ and light qāf, making God the one who brings out the open record.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r3.anchor: وهو نافع وابن كثير وعامة قراء العراق {ونخرج} [الإسراء: 13] بالنون {له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا} [الإسراء: 13]

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r4.speaker: قراؤ أهل الشام
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r4.claim: Some Syrian readers share the nūn reading of wa-nukhriju but read yulaqqāhu passively with a doubled qāf, so the person is handed the record.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r4.anchor: وكان بعض قراء أهل الشام يوافق هؤلاء على قراءة قوله {ونخرج} [الإسراء: 13] ويخالفهم في قوله {يلقاه} [الإسراء: 13] فيقرؤه: «يلقاه» بضم الياء وتشديد القاف،

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r5.claim: Mujāhid reads wa-yukhraju lahu; al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī and Ibn Muḥayṣin also read it this way, construing the assigned bird as becoming a book the person reads.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه قرأها (ويخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا) قال: يزيد: يعني يخرج الطائر كتابا هكذا أحسبه قرأها بفتح الياء،

TAB-FULL:v14p520/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r6.claim: The author prefers the nūn form wa-nukhriju and active yalqāhu because the preceding clause names God as the one who binds the person's destiny, so the next clause should keep God as subject.
TAB-FULL:v14p520/r6.anchor: وأولى القراءات في ذلك بالصواب، قراءة من قرأه: {ونخرج} [الإسراء: 13] بالنون وضمها

TAB-FULL:v14p523/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r1.claim: On the preferred reading, God will bring each person an open register listing their worldly deeds and assigned destiny, fully accounting for everything done.
