TAB-FULL:v14p523/r1.anchor: ونحن نخرج له إذا وافانا كتابا يصادفه منشورا بأعماله التي عملها في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v14p523/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the open book as the person's recorded deeds, displayed on the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، {ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا} [الإسراء: 13] قال: هو عمله الذي عمل أحصي عليه،

TAB-FULL:v14p523/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r3.claim: Qatāda likewise says the open register is the person's deeds.
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه منشورا} [الإسراء: 13] أي عمله

TAB-FULL:v14p523/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says two recording angels, one on each side, write good and bad deeds; at death the scroll is rolled up and placed with the person in the grave, then brought out open at resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v14p523/r4.anchor: فأما الذي عن يمينك فيحفظ حسناتك. وأما الذي عن شمالك فيحفظ سيئاتك،

TAB-FULL:v14p524/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r1.claim: Qatāda calls the attached bird one's deed and says that deed is brought out as an open book.
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r1.anchor: عن قتادة: طائره: عمله، ونخرج له بذلك العمل كتابا يلقاه منشورا

TAB-FULL:v14p524/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r2.claim: A grammarian's alternative takes the bird as one's allotted share, from an arrow falling to someone's lot; the author says this is possible, but exegetical consensus should guide interpretation, and it agrees if the share means one's deeds, misery, and happiness.
TAB-FULL:v14p524/r2.anchor: من قولهم: طار سهم فلان بكذا: إذا خرج سهمه على نصيب من الأنصباء،

TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r5.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r5.claim: Al-Majmaʿ says a person’s bird is his deed, likened to birds used for omens: a sanīḥ passes from left to right auspiciously, while a bāriḥ passes right to left ominously.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r5.anchor: الطائر هنا عمل الإنسان شبه بالطائر الذي يسنح ويتبرك به

TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r6.speaker: أبو زيد
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r6.claim: Abū Zayd says Arabs call anything that passes by, bird or gazelle, a ṭāʾir in this omen practice.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r6.anchor: كل ما يجري من طائر أو ظبي أو غيره فهو عندهم طائر

TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r7.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf says travelers would make birds fly: passage from left to right was a good omen, from right to left a bad omen, hence taṭayyur.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#5/r7.anchor: فإذا سافروا ومر بهم طير زجروه فإن مر بهم سانحا بأن مر من جهة اليسار إلى اليمين تيمنوا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r1.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r1.claim: The lexicon derives omen-taking from divination by birds, then extends it to anything treated as a good or bad omen.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r1.anchor: تطير فلان واطير أصله التفاؤل بالطير ثم يستعمل في كل ما يتفاءل به ويتشاءم

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r2.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r2.claim: The verb for people dispersing can also mean that they hurry.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r2.anchor: ويقال تطايروا إذا أسرعوا ويقال إذا تفرقوا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r3.claim: In context, a person's bird is what indicates the good or bad outcome awaiting him.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r3.anchor: سياق ما قبل الآية وما بعدها وخاصة قوله { من اهتدى فإنما يهتدي لنفسه } الخ

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r4.claim: The neck signifies attachment because a person cannot separate from it, unlike the limbs, and anything hung there immediately faces him.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r4.anchor: وإنما جعل الإلزام في العنق لأنه العضو الذي لا يمكن أن يفارقه الإنسان

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r5.claim: The attached bird is each person's acquired deed, which remains with him and determines his felicity or misery by God's decree.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r5.anchor: فالمراد بقوله { وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه } أن الذي يستعقب لكل إنسان سعادته أو شقاءه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r6.claim: A person's deed belongs to that person, who receives its full recompense, as the cited passage on human striving says.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r6.anchor: وهذا هو العمل الذي يعمله الإنسان لقوله تعالى

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r7.claim: The ordained pattern makes good outcomes follow faith and piety, and bad outcomes follow disbelief and disobedience.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r7.anchor: أن حسن العاقبة للإيمان والتقوى وسوء العاقبة للكفر والمعصية

TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r8.claim: The verse ties felicity and misery to freely acquired good and bad deeds; it does not endorse an eternal decree independent of whether one acts or obeys.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#6/r8.anchor: من جهة أعماله الحسنة والسيئة المكتسبة من طريق الاختيار من دون أن يبطل تأثير العمل

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.claim: The displayed book is each person's own record and contains every deed without omission.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r1.anchor: أن الكتاب الذي يخرج له هو كتابه نفسه لا يتعلق بغيره

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.claim: The record shows deeds in their true realities, with their good or evil results exposed beyond concealment or excuse.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r2.anchor: وثالثا أن الأعمال التي أحصاها بادية فيها بحقائقها من سعادة أو شقاء

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.claim: The record contains the actual deeds themselves, made visible to the person, rather than written symbols like ordinary books.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r3.anchor: أن الكتاب يتضمن نفس الأعمال بحقائقها دون الرسوم المخطوطة على حد الكتب المعمولة فيما بيننا

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.claim: The bird and book refer to the same deed; calling it a book at resurrection avoids suggesting it only then becomes a book or was previously hidden despite clinging to its owner.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r4.anchor: أن المراد بالطائر والكتاب في الآية أمر واحد وهو العمل الذي يعمله الإنسان

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.claim: God brings the book out from behind heedlessness on Judgment Day and makes its details visible, already prepared for its owner.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r5.anchor: كتاب الأعمال بحقائقها مستور عن إدراك الإنسان محجوب وراء حجاب الغفلة

TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.claim: The book confirms that a person will inevitably meet the consequences of his deeds, since they both cling to him and will be openly displayed.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#7/r6.anchor: الإنسان ستناله تبعة عمله لا محالة أما أولا فلأنه لازم له لا يفارقه

TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.claim: The surrounding rebuke links human haste to the record of deeds: people fail to distinguish benefit from harm and rush after desires, though every deed remains with its doer and will be reviewed.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r1.anchor: أنزل القرآن وجعله هاديا إلى ملة هي أقوم جريا على السنة الإلهية في هداية الناس

TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r2.speaker: المفردات
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r2.claim: The word وزر means a burden, metaphorically used for sin as a burden to carry.
TABATABAI:17:9-22#8/r2.anchor: الوزر الثقل تشبيها بوزر الجبل، ويعبر بذلك عن الإثم كما يعبر عنه بالثقل

TABATABAI:17:22#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r6.claim: In a report through Abu al-Jarud, Abu Jaʿfar says a person's good and evil remain with him wherever he goes until he receives the record of his deeds.
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r6.anchor: وفي رواية أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام

TABATABAI:17:22#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r7.claim: A report from Zurarah, Humran, and Muhammad ibn Muslim, citing Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abd Allah, explains the attached bird as a person's allotted measure or destiny.
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r7.anchor: عن زرارة وحمران ومحمد بن مسلم عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليهما السلام عن الآية

TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.claim: The author omits reports on these verses transmitted through both Sunni and Shiʿi routes from the Prophet, Ali, Salman, and others because they lack Quranic, prophetic, or decisive rational support and have weak chains.
TABATABAI:17:22#2/r10.anchor: روايات تركنا إيرادها لعدم تأيدها بكتاب أو سنة أو حجة عقلية قاطعة مع ما فيها من ضعف الأسناد

TABRISI:17:13-15/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:17:13-15/r1.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads ويخرج with passive yāʾ; Yaʿqūb reads it with active yāʾ, while the others use nūn.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر ويخرج له بضم الياء وفتح الراء

TABRISI:17:13-15/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر
TABRISI:17:13-15/r2.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir read تُلَقِّيه with tāʾ; the others read يلقاه with yāʾ.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر تلقيه بضم التاء

TABRISI:17:13-15/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r3.claim: On both yāʾ readings, the person's work or fate is brought out or comes out as a book, with كتابا circumstantial.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r3.anchor: فمعناه أنه يخرج له عمله أو يخرج له طائره يوم القيامة

TABRISI:17:13-15/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r4.claim: With nūn, كتابا is the object, a specification, or a circumstantial phrase meaning accompanied by a book in which deeds are recorded.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r4.anchor: فيكون كتابا مفعولا لنخرج ويجوز أن يكون منصوبا على التمييز

TABRISI:17:13-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r5.claim: منشورا is circumstantial across the readings; yلقاه evokes pages being unfolded, while the alternate phrase is illustrated by a verse about greeting.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r5.anchor: منشورا يكون منصوبا على الحال من الهاء في يلقاه

TABRISI:17:13-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r6.claim: Insān is common gender like faras; separate words distinguish male and female animals.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r6.anchor: الإنسان يقع على المذكر والمؤنث فإذا أردت الفصل

TABRISI:17:13-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r7.claim: Basrans derive insān from sociability or humanness on faʿlān; Kufans derive it from forgetfulness, originally insiyān with yāʾ omitted for ease.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r7.anchor: واشتقاق الإنسان من الإنس أو الأنس وهو فعلان عند البصريين

TABRISI:17:13-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r8.claim: Kufans cite the diminutive unaysiyān; Basrans treat its yāʾ as extra and the diminutive as irregular, like other listed examples.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r8.anchor: واحتجوا على ذلك بقول العرب في تصغيره إنيسيان

TABRISI:17:13-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r9.claim: Ṭāʾir means human deeds or fate, likened to an auspicious or inauspicious bird passing right or left.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r9.anchor: والطائر ها هنا عمل الإنسان شبه بالطائر الذي يسنح

TABRISI:17:13-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15/r10.claim: A sāniḥ moves from one's right to left and is auspicious because a hunter can aim; a bāriḥ crosses the other way and is difficult to aim at.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r10.anchor: والسانح الذي يجعل ميامنه إلى مياسرك والبارح الذي يجعل مياسره

TABRISI:17:13-15/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15/r11.speaker: أبو زيد
TABRISI:17:13-15/r11.claim: Abū Zayd says any passing bird, gazelle, or creature is called ṭāʾir; the source begins a poem by Kathīr as evidence but the excerpt ends before its verse.
TABRISI:17:13-15/r11.anchor: قال أبو زيد ما يجري من طائر أو ظبي أو غيره فهو عندهم طائر

TABRISI:17:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13/r1.claim: Arab usage treats consulting a bird as an omen from its flight, good or bad; the cited poetry illustrates this divinatory idiom.
TABRISI:17:13/r1.anchor: قال وقولهم سألت الطير وقلت للطير إنما هو زجرتها من خير أو شر

TABRISI:17:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13/r2.claim: The bird is placed at the neck because deeds stay attached like a collar; Arabic also uses body parts for the whole person.
TABRISI:17:13/r2.anchor: وإنما قال طائره في عنقه ولم يقل في يده لينبه على لزوم ذلك له

TABRISI:17:13/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
TABRISI:17:13/r3.claim: Saying someone's neck or throat is free emancipates them because it means the whole body; saying hand or hair is free does not.
TABRISI:17:13/r3.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: إذا قال الإنسان عنقك أو رقبتك حر عتق

TABRISI:17:13/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13/r4.speaker: الشافعي
TABRISI:17:13/r4.claim: He treats such expressions alike and says either declaration emancipates.
TABRISI:17:13/r4.anchor: وقال الشافعي: هما سواء يعتق في الحالين.

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r1.claim: He explains the bird as a person's good or ill omen; the verse echoes bird-omen expressions in the messengers' story and Pharaoh's people.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r1.anchor: وقيل طائره يمنه وشؤمه عن الحسن وهو ما يتطير منه

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة والقتيبي
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r2.claim: They understand the bird as a person's share of good and evil.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r2.anchor: وقيل طائره حظه من الخير والشر عن أبي عبدة والقتيبي

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the bird to mean the book of deeds; another says each person is his own guide and witness.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r3.anchor: وقيل طائره كتابه وقيل معناه جعلنا لكل إنسان دليلا من نفسه

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r4.claim: The record is written by guardian angels and presented open for its owner to see and read; the pronoun 'for him' can refer to the person or the deed.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r4.anchor: وهو ما كتبه الحفظة عليهم من أعمالهم { يلقاه } أي يرى ذلك الكتاب

TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.claim: A person will recall all recorded deeds as if doing them at that moment, explaining the comparison with the record in al-Kahf.
TABRISI:17:13-15#2/r6.anchor: وروى جابر بن خالد بن نجيح عن أبي عبد الله ع قال: يذكر العبد جميع أعماله

THALABI:v6p88/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p88/r1.claim: A person’s allotted good and evil remain attached to him wherever he goes.
THALABI:v6p88/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وما قدر عليه

THALABI:v6p88/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r2.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
THALABI:v6p88/r2.claim: Good and evil accompany a person until he is reckoned for them.
THALABI:v6p88/r2.anchor: الكلبي ومقاتل: خيره وشره معه لا يفارقه حتى يحاسب به

THALABI:v6p88/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v6p88/r3.claim: Hasan recites that recording angels sit at a person’s right and left; his open record accompanies him through life, is folded at death, and reopened at resurrection.
THALABI:v6p88/r3.anchor: وتلا الحسن: عن اليمين وعن الشمال قعيد] ثم قال يا بن آدم بسطت لك صحيفتك

THALABI:v6p88/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p88/r4.claim: The attached bird signifies a person’s deeds and provision.
THALABI:v6p88/r4.anchor: مجاهد: عمله ورزقه، وعنه: ما من مولود يولد

THALABI:v6p88/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p88/r5.claim: Every newborn has a paper at his neck recording whether he is blessed or wretched.
THALABI:v6p88/r5.anchor: مجاهد: عمله ورزقه، وعنه: ما من مولود يولد إلا وفي عنقه ورقة

THALABI:v6p88/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v6p88/r6.claim: The bird represents what a person is destined to do and become, whether happy or wretched.
THALABI:v6p88/r6.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: أراد بالطائر ما قضى عليه

THALABI:v6p88/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r7.speaker: أهل المعاني
THALABI:v6p88/r7.claim: The destiny is called a bird by analogy with Arab omens drawn from birds flying to the right or left.
THALABI:v6p88/r7.anchor: وإنما عبر عنه بالطائر على عادة العرب كما كانت تتفاءل به

THALABI:v6p88/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد والعيني
THALABI:v6p88/r8.claim: The bird means one’s share of good or evil, as in the Arab idiom that someone’s bird flew with a certain lot.
THALABI:v6p88/r8.anchor: أبو عبيد والعيني: أراد بالطائر حظه من الخير والشر

THALABI:v6p88/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r9.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء
THALABI:v6p88/r9.claim: They read طئره without the alif; the neck is singled out because marks and ornaments are placed there and Arabs assign lasting things to the neck.
THALABI:v6p88/r9.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ومجاهد وأبو رجاء: طئره في عنقه بغير ألف

THALABI:v6p88/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p88/r10.claim: The neck is singled out as the place of marks, necklaces, and things that adorn or disfigure, matching Arab idioms for an inescapable duty.
THALABI:v6p88/r10.anchor: لأن العنق موضع السمات وموضع القلائد والأطراف وغير ذلك مما يشين أو يزين

THALABI:v6p88/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r11.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب
THALABI:v6p88/r11.claim: They read ويخرج with open yāʾ and damma on rāʾ, making the person’s bird bring out a book; كتابًا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative.
THALABI:v6p88/r11.anchor: قرأ الحسن ومجاهد وابن محيصن ويعقوب: ويخرج بفتح الياء وضم الراء

THALABI:v6p88/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p88/r12.claim: An alternative construal has the person’s bird emerge and become a book.
THALABI:v6p88/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه ويخرج له الطائر فيصير كتابا

THALABI:v6p88/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r13.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v6p88/r13.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads the verb passively, meaning that the bird is brought out as a book.
THALABI:v6p88/r13.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: ويخرج بضم الياء وفتح الراء

THALABI:v6p88/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r14.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
THALABI:v6p88/r14.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb reads an active form with God as its understood subject.
THALABI:v6p88/r14.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب: ويخرج أي ويخرج الله

THALABI:v6p88/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p88/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p88/r15.claim: The remaining readers use first-person plural and take كتابًا as the object; Abū ʿAmr supports this from ألزمناه, though the citation is cut off.
THALABI:v6p88/r15.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بنون مضمومة وكسر الراء على معنى ونحن نخرج له

THALABI:v6p89/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r1.speaker: أبو عامر وأبو جعفر
THALABI:v6p89/r1.claim: They read تلقاه with tāʾ and doubled qāf, meaning the person is given the book; others use yāʾ, meaning he sees it.
THALABI:v6p89/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عامر وأبو جعفر: تلقاه بضم التاء وتشديد القاف

THALABI:v6p89/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p89/r2.claim: منشورًا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative, describing the book as open.

THALABI:v6p89/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p89/r3.speaker: أبو السوار العدوي
THALABI:v6p89/r3.claim: A person’s record is open in life, folded at death, and reopened at resurrection, so he should fill it as he chooses while alive.
THALABI:v6p89/r3.anchor: يا ابن آدم فصحيفتك منشورة فاعمل فيها ما شئت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r1.claim: In al-Ḥakam's report, Mujāhid says each person's record of misery or felicity is written on a sheet hanging from the neck.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r1.anchor: روى الحكم عن مجاهد قال: مكتوب في ورقة شقي أو سعيد معلقة في عنقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the bird fastened to the neck as a person's misery and felicity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r2.anchor: وهذا كما روي عن الحسن في قوله: {طائره في عنقه} قال: شقاوته وسعادته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid says the bird means one's deeds, whether they bring misery or felicity.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r3.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: عمله من شقاوة أو سعادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r4.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī interprets it as whatever good or evil has been written for the person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: ما كتب له من خير أو شر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a person's work and allotted fate remain with him wherever he goes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r5.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أنه قال عمله وما قدر عليه فهو ملازمه أينما كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r6.claim: The Arabs called good or bad fortune a bird because of their augury; the source then names poetry by Ḥassān and Kathīr witnessing the bird/omen idiom, while condemning augury as pre-Islamic falsehood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r6.anchor: ذريني وعلمي بالأمور وسيرتي ... فما طائري فيها عليك بأخيلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r7.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r7.claim: Their reading ṭayrihi supports interpreting the bird as one's own deed, good or bad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p274#2/r7.anchor: قراءة الحسن ومجاهد: (ألزمناه طيره في عنقه)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r1.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says bird means a person's deeds in Arabic usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r1.anchor: قال الفراء: الطائر معناه عندهم العمل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says ṭāʾir means one's lot, like the Persian bakht, or what falls to someone when property is apportioned; see 7:131.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الطائر عند العرب الحظ

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r3.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r3.claim: Al-Azharī links each person's fate to God's primordial knowledge and writing of obedient and disobedient descendants of Adam.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p277/r3.anchor: قال الأزهري: والأصل في هذا أن الله تعالى لما خلق آدم علم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r1.claim: Being in the neck expresses attachment, like a necklace that remains on its wearer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r1.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: وإنما يقال للشيء اللازم: هذا في عنق فلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī compares this idiom to assigning or saddling something on someone; the attached poem by al-Aʿshā illustrates the usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r2.anchor: وقال أبو علي: وهذا مثل قولهم: طوقتك كذا وقلدتك كذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r3.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r3.claim: Some exegetes say the neck is specified because good deeds adorn like jewelry while bad deeds disfigure like a fetter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r3.anchor: إنما خص العنق؛ لأن عمله لا يخلو إما أن يكون خيرا يزينه أو شرا يشينه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r4.claim: On Mujāhid's sheet interpretation, the allotted fate is fixed in a sheet hung at the neck but is not visibly observed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p278/r4.anchor: ما قسم له أثبت في ورقة وعلقت من عنقه، غير أنا لا نشاهد ذلك مرئيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r1.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan describes two recording angels, one preserving good deeds and one sins; the folded record accompanies the person in the grave and is brought out at resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r1.anchor: بسطت لك صحيفة، ووكل بك ملكان، فهما عن يمينك وعن شمالك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r2.claim: The record may be brought out from the person's grave, or the verb may mean that God reveals it after it was unseen in worldly life.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r2.anchor: فعلى هذا معنى: {ونخرج له}، أي: من قبره معه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r3.speaker: يعقوب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r3.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb passively; the person's bird, meaning his deed, is brought out as a record entered in the comprehensive book of 18:49.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r3.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب: (ويخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar has the same reading and takes the deed-record as a scroll spread open, as in 81:10.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r4.anchor: وعلى هذا المعنى قرأ أبو جعفر (¬2): (ويخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r5.speaker: ابن عامر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yulaqqāhu, meaning the person is met with the record; the wording is a causative form, as in 76:11.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p279/r5.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: (يلقاه) (¬4) من قولهم: لقيت فلانا

SAMIN-DURR:17:13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:13/r3.claim: A reading lightens عنقه, a common phonetic simplification.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13/r3.anchor: وقرئ " في عنقه " وهو تخفيف شائع

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r1.claim: The common reading has نخرج from أخرج; كتابا is either its object or circumstantial after an omitted object, with the bird's omen understood.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r1.anchor: العامة على " نخرج " بنون العظمة مضارع " اخرج "

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r2.claim: Abu Ja'far reports passive يخرج with كتابا circumstantial and the bird's pronoun as passive subject; he also reports nominative كتابا, which the author calls awkward.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن أبي جعفر: " ويخرج " مبنيا للمفعول، " كتابا " نصب على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan reads يخرج with open yā and damma rā from خرج, making كتاب the subject.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: " ويخرج " بفتح الياء وضم الراء مضارع " خرج "

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r4.speaker: ابن محيصن، مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r4.claim: They have the same verb reading but make كتابا circumstantial: the person's omen emerges to him as a book.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r4.anchor: وابن محيصن ومجاهد كذلك، إلا أنهما نصبا " كتابا " على الحال

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r5.claim: Another reading has يُخرج from أخرج, with God as subject and كتابا as object.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r5.anchor: وقرئ " ويخرج " بضم الياء وكسر الراء مضارع " اخرج "

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r6.speaker: الزمخشري، الشيخ، أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r6.claim: They allow منشورا as an adjective of كتاب; the author objects that this puts a less explicit adjective before an explicit one.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r6.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري والشيخ وأبو البقاء أن يكون نعتا لكتاب. وفيه نظر

SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r7.speaker: ابن عامر
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r7.claim: Ibn Amir reads يلقاه with doubled qāf, from the intensive form of لقي; the others read the simple active form لقي.
SAMIN-DURR:17:13#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر " يلقاه " بضم الياء وفتح اللام وتشديد القاف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r5.claim: Each person's assigned record is what he does, both good and evil.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r5.anchor: كتبنا عليه ما يعمل من خير وشر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r6.claim: On Resurrection Day, each person's record of deeds is brought out and displayed open.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:17:12-14/r6.anchor: ونخرج له } ونظهر له { يوم القيامة } صحيفة عمله منشورة.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r6.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains each person’s “bird” attached to the neck as that person’s deeds.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r6.anchor: قوله: {وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه} [الإسراء: 13] المبارك بن فضالة عن الحسن قال: عمله.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r7.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r7.claim: Qatāda gives the same interpretation: the attached bird is a person’s deeds.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.claim: Qatāda says even those who could not read in worldly life will read their record at the Resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r8.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة، قال: سيقرأ يومئذ من لم يكن قارئا في الدنيا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that people are summoned for judgment; one who led many people toward good is called by name and given a record with sins inside and good deeds on its back.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r9.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، قال: يدعى الخلائق يوم القيامة للحساب، فإذا كان الرجل في الخير رأسا يدعو إليه،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.claim: In Ubayy’s account, the person first fears the sins, then finds them forgiven; his good deeds are doubled, his face brightens, he is adorned and given the book in his right hand.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r10.anchor: فيبدأ بالسيئات فيقرأها فيشفق ويتغير لونه، فإذا بلغ آخر الكتاب وجد فيه: هذه سيئاتك وقد غفرت لك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.claim: The honored person is given a crown, two garments, ornaments at every joint, and a stature of sixty cubits, identified as Adam’s height.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r11.anchor: ويؤتى بتاج فيوضع على رأسه، ويكسى حلتين، ويحلى كل مفصل منه، ويطول ستين ذراعا، وهي قامة آدم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.speaker: أبي بن كعب
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.claim: He is told to go announce the same reward to his companions, quotes 69:19–23, and explains that God’s honor changed his appearance when they ask who he is.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p120/r12.anchor: فيقال له: انطلق إلى أصحابك فبشرهم وأخبرهم أن لكل إنسان منهم مثل هذا.

ELMALILI:17:13-14/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r1.claim: Every person’s bird tied to the neck signifies one’s fate or share of good and evil from the unseen, assigned to one’s own responsibility and choices, or the burden of one’s own sins.
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r1.anchor: baht u kaderini, âlem-i gaybdan uçup gelecek olan hayır veya şer nasibini kendi zimmetine ilzam eyledik

ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.claim: At resurrection each person receives an opened record of deeds and account and is told to read it; the self is sufficient as its own accountant.
ELMALILI:17:13-14/r2.anchor: bir kitap -a‘mâlini kayd ve hesâbını irâe eden bir defter- çıkaracağız

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r1.claim: Tair literally means bird and refers metaphorically to responsibility; pre-Islamic bird divination made it signify luck, while commentators also offered fate, good and evil, deeds, provision, and obligation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r2.claim: Among the proposed meanings, the commentary prefers deeds and obligations, rendered as responsibility, a reading reinforced by the following reference to the record book.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r2.anchor: diye ifade etmek daha uygun düşmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.claim: Each person is bound by their own actions and will see the result when the record of deeds is opened.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r3.anchor: her insan yaptığı ile kendini bağlamış, sorumluluk altına girmiştir, sonucunu da önüne amel defteri konularak görecektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.claim: After the discussion of revelation, faith, reward, and punishment, there is no excuse: each person bears responsibility and is told to read their own record and judge themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:17:13/r4.anchor: Bütün bunlardan sonra 13. âyette artık insanlar için mazeret kalmadığı belirtilmek üzere, mahşer meydanında toplanan herkesin sorumluluğunun kendi omuzunda olacağı

ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r6.claim: Both accusative and nominative are grammatically possible for كل in this clause, though the author knows no reader who used the nominative.
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r6.anchor: وكذلك النصب والرفع في قوله: (وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه) إلا إني لا أعلم أحدا قرأ بالرفع

ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r7.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r7.claim: The gloss for a person's طائر is their good and evil.
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r7.anchor: وجاء في التفسير: طائره، أي خيره وشره

ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r8.claim: The author explains طائر as what a person brings upon himself through his deeds; it remains attached like a necklace, as in the saying that one's sin is on another's neck.
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r8.anchor: وهو - والله أعلم - ما يتطير من مثله من شيء عمله كما قال

ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r9.claim: The wording has four reported forms: ونخرج له, ويخرج له with God as subject, and ويخرج له with the person's deeds as the subject or referent.
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r9.anchor: وفي هذه أربعة أوجه: وتخرج له، ويخرج له، أي ويخرج الله له

ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p230/r10.claim: كتابا is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier describing what he meets spread open.

ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r1.claim: Ta'ir literally means bird or flying creature and became a term for omen, fortune, or destiny because Arabs read the future from birds' flight.
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r1.anchor: the term ta'ir came to be tropically used in the sense of "fortune", both good and evil, or "destiny"

ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r2.claim: Qur'anic destiny concerns the moral direction a person chooses, not chiefly external events; inclinations, attitudes, actions, and omissions shape one's spiritual fate, for which God holds each person responsible.
ASAD-NOTES:17:13#n17/r2.anchor: man's spiritual fate depends on himself and is inseparably linked with the whole tenor of his personality

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r1.claim: Ṭāʾir in the neck means a person’s deed or fate remains attached to him like a collar or chain.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p89/r2.claim: The book in wa-nukhriju lahu kitāban is a direct object; “yulqāhu spread open” is supported by the verse about opened scrolls.

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p214#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p214#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p214#2/r1.claim: With light qāf and still lām, the book itself meets the person; with doubled qāf and open lām, the verb is passive and the pronoun refers to the book.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p214#2/r1.anchor: بتخفيف القاف وسكون اللام وبتشديدها وفتح اللام

IBNMUJAHID:v1p378/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p378/r3.speaker: author
IBNMUJAHID:v1p378/r3.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads yulqīhi with ḍamma yāʾ and doubled qāf; the others use yalqīhi with fatḥa yāʾ, quiescent lām, and light qāf. Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī apply imāla to qāf.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p378/r3.anchor: 3 واختلفوا فى قوله ﴿ ونخرج له يوم القيامة كتابا يلقاه ﴾ 13

QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#1/r1.claim: The passive reading presents the record as brought forth without naming God as its agent.
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#1/r1.anchor: shifts from active divine production to passive unveiling

QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#2/r1.claim: The intransitive Form I makes the record come out by itself, without an external agent.
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:9#2/r1.anchor: no external agent at all; kitāb becomes self-emerging, autonomous

QIRAAT-ER:17:13:14#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:14#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:14#1/r1.claim: The passive Form II reading implies an intermediary delivers the record, rather than the person finding it directly.
QIRAAT-ER:17:13:14#1/r1.anchor: canonical variant that adds intermediary: someone causes the encounter rather than the human finding it directly

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r1.claim: A person's attached bird is their deed, which will be brought out as an open book.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ﴾ قال عمله ويخرج ذلك العمل كتابا يلقاه منشورا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r2.claim: Hasan says a person's bird is their deed, whether it brings misery or felicity.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p374#4/r2.anchor: قال معمر وقال الحسن طائره عمله شقاوة أو سعادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses طائره as what is decreed for or against a person.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ما قدر له وعليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r2.speaker: مجاهد، قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r2.claim: Mujāhid and Qatāda say bird conveys a person’s allotted fortune and work through Arab belief in omens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r2.anchor: فعبر عن الحظ والعمل إذ هما متلازمان بالطائر قاله مجاهد وقتادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r3.claim: The verse corrects bird-omen beliefs: each person’s good, evil, lot, work, and acquisition are fixed and attached to the neck.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r3.anchor: فأخبرهم الله تعالى في أوجز لفظ وأبلغ إشارة أن جميع ما يلقى الإنسان من خير وشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، السدي، أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r4.claim: They gloss طائره respectively as deed, book, and fortune called bakht.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r4.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: طائره عمله، وعن السدي كتابه الذي يطير إليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan compares the record to a page tied around the neck at resurrection; the neck bears ornaments or disgrace like a shackle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r5.anchor: وعن الحسن: يا ابن آدم بسطت لك صحيفة إذا بعثت قلدتها في عنقك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r6.speaker: مجاهد، الحسن، أبو رجاء، الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r6.claim: Some read طيره and a quiescent nūn in عنقه; the majority reads active ونخرج with accusative كتابا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r6.anchor: وقرأ مجاهد والحسن وأبو رجاء طيره. وقرىء: في عنقه بسكون النون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر، الحسن، ابن محيصن، مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r7.claim: Abū Jaʿfar has a passive يخرج with accusative كتابا or raised كتاب; another group reads active يخرج, with al-Ḥasan making كتاب the subject.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r7.anchor: وعن أبي جعفر أيضا ويخرج بالياء مبنيا للمفعول كتابا أي ويخرج الطائر كتابا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r8.speaker: الجمهور، ابن عامر، أبو جعفر، الجحدري، الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r8.claim: The majority reads يلقاه; the named readers also report a form with doubled qāf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يلقاه بفتح الياء وسكون اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p21/r9.claim: منشورا means unfolded for reading; يلقاه and منشورا may describe the book or the latter may be circumstantial.

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r1.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r1.claim: Anas reports from the Prophet that whoever seeks refuge ten times in a day is assigned an angel by God to drive Satan away.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r1.anchor: روى أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : من استعاذ في اليوم عشر مرات وكل الله تعالى به ملكا يذود عنه الشيطان

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r2.claim: Understanding the invocation reveals one's limited power and knowledge, discourages obeying the self's prompts, and thereby wards off the greater Satan, the self.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r2.anchor: والسبب فيه أنه لما قال { أعوذ بالله } وعرف معناه عرف منه نقصان قدرته ونقصان علمه

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r3.speaker: خولة بنت حكيم
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r3.claim: Khawla bint Hakim reports from the Prophet that whoever alights somewhere and seeks refuge in God's perfect words from created evil will be unharmed until departing.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r3.anchor: عن خولة بنت حكيم عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : من نزل منزلا فقال أعوذ بكلمات الله التامات

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r4.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r4.claim: Razi cites the Prophet's statement that heaven groans, with no place for a foot that lacks an angel standing or sitting there.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r4.anchor: كما قال عليه الصلاة والسلام أطت السماء وحق لها أن تئط ما فيها موضع قدم إلا وفيه ملك قائم أو قاعد

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r5.claim: The heavens, ether, and air contain numerous pure and harmful spirits; invoking God's perfect words seeks aid from pure spirits against wicked ones.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r5.anchor: وكذلك الأثير والهواء مملوءة من الأرواح وبعضها طاهرة مشرقة خيرة وبعضها كدرة مؤذية شريرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r6.claim: Alternatively, God's words are His command Be, expressing effective power; refuge in God's power protects from every harm.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r6.anchor: كلمات الله هي قوله كن وهي عبارة عن القدرة النافذة ومن استعاذ بقدرة الله لم يضره شيء

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r7.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r7.claim: The Prophet teaches a frightened sleeper to seek refuge from divine anger, punishment, evil servants, and satanic prompts; the utterance protects.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r7.anchor: عن عمرو بن شعيب عن أبيه عن جده أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : إذا فزع أحدكم من النوم

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r8.claim: Ibn Umar taught the invocation to slaves old enough to understand and wrote it on paper to hang around the necks of those too young.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r8.anchor: وكان عبد الله بن عمر يعلمها من بلغ من عبيده ومن لم يبلغ كتبها في صك ثم علقها في عنقه

RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet sought protection for Hasan and Husayn in God's perfect words from every devil and poisonous creature.
RAZI-FULL:v1p69/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : أنه كان يعوذ الحسن والحسين رضي الله عنهما

BURHAN:v2p205/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p205/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p205/r7.claim: The bird bound to each person’s neck cannot be literal; it means each person is assigned their own book in the reckoning.
BURHAN:v2p205/r7.anchor: وكقوله ﴿ وكل إنسان ألزمناه طائره في عنقه ﴾ يستحيل ان يشد في القيامة في عنق كل طائع وعاص وغيرهما طير من الطيور فوجب حمله على التزام الكتاب

BURHAN:v4p317/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r1.claim: كل names the encompassing combination of a thing’s parts, and is explained through words for objects that surround something.
BURHAN:v4p317/r1.anchor: اسم وضع لضم أجزاء الشيء على جهة الإحاطة من حيث كان لفظه مأخوذا

BURHAN:v4p317/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r3.claim: With an indefinite complement, كل ranges over its individuals; with a definite complement, it may range over all parts of what it modifies.
BURHAN:v4p317/r3.anchor: ثم إن دخل على منكر أوجب عموم افراد المضاف إليه أو على معرف أوجب عموم أجزاء ما دخل عليه

BURHAN:v4p317/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r5.claim: كل is always annexed in meaning, although its complement may be omitted from the wording except in emphatic or adjectival uses.
BURHAN:v4p317/r5.anchor: وهو لازم للإضافة معنى ولا يلزم إضافته لفظا إلا إذا وقع تأكيدا أو نعتا

BURHAN:v4p317/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.claim: Its overt complement may be a definite plural, generic noun, pronoun, or indefinite singular.
BURHAN:v4p317/r6.anchor: ويضاف تارة إلى الجمع المعرف نحو

BURHAN:v4p317/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.claim: When no complement appears, it is understood; scholars differ whether its tanwin substitutes for the complement or is ordinary declension.
BURHAN:v4p317/r7.anchor: وربما خلا من الإضافة لفظا وينوي فيه

BURHAN:v4p317/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p317/r8.speaker: أبو الفتح
BURHAN:v4p317/r8.claim: Abu al-Fath prefers placing كل before its governing word because it resembles an initial subject and avoids direct government over it.
BURHAN:v4p317/r8.anchor: قال أبو الفتح وتقديمها أحسن من تأخيرها لأن التقدير كلهم فلو أخرت لباشرت العوامل

BURHAN:v4p320/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p320/r2.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p320/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli says detached كل must be a subject, a subject followed by its verb, or governed by a preposition attached to what follows; context must supply its scope.
BURHAN:v4p320/r2.anchor: وأما المقطوع عن الإضافة فقال السهيلي حقها إن تكون مبتدأة مخبرا عنها أو مبتدأة منصوبة بفعل بعدها لا قبلها

BURHAN:v4p320/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p320/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p320/r3.claim: Although كل is masculine singular in form, agreement follows the meaning of its complement.
BURHAN:v4p320/r3.anchor: واعلم إن لفظ كل لأفراد التذكير ومعناه بحسب ما يضاف إليه والأحوال ثلاثة

BURHAN:v4p320/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p320/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p320/r4.claim: With an indefinite noun, agreement can follow its sense: masculine singular for person or thing, feminine singular for soul, and masculine plural for a collective party.
BURHAN:v4p320/r4.anchor: فالأول إن يضاف إلى نكرة فيجب مراعاة معناها فلذلك جاء الضمير مفردامذكرا في قوله تعالى ﴿ وكل شيء فعلوه في الزبر ﴾ 3 ﴿ وكل إنسان ألزمناه ﴾ 4

BURHAN:v2p77/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p77/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p77/r1.claim: Clear verses aid argument with a religious opponent because their apparent sense counters his claim and redirects him from ambiguity and rational doubts toward transmitted evidence.
BURHAN:v2p77/r1.anchor: وللمحكم في باب الحجاج عند غير المخالف مزية لأنه لا يمكن أن يبين له أنه مخالف للقرآن وأن ظاهر المحكم يدل على خلاف ما ذهب إليه

BURHAN:v1p288/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p288/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p288/r5.claim: Al-sijill is listed as a Persian word for a book.

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r1.claim: Kull denotes all individuals of an indefinite noun to which it is annexed, all members of a definite plural, or all parts of a definite singular.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r1.anchor: اسم موضوع لاستغراق أفراد المنكر المضاف هو إليه

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r2.claim: Kull can modify a noun to express completeness, emphasize a definite noun for totality, or follow an operator as a noun; its construction changes with each function.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r2.anchor: أحدها أن تكون نعتا لنكرة أو معرفة فتدل على كماله

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r3.claim: When kull is annexed to an indefinite, agreement in its pronoun must follow its meaning, as in 'every human'.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r3.anchor: وحيث أضيفت إلى منكر وجب في ضميرها مراعاة معناها نحو

ITQAN:v2p492#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r6.claim: When a negative particle or verb governs kull, the negation is directed specifically at comprehensiveness.
ITQAN:v2p492#3/r6.anchor: وحيث وقعت في حيز النفي بأن تقدمت عليها أداته أو الفعل المنفي فالنفي موجه إلى الشمول خاصة

ITQAN:v4p452/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p452/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p452/r1.claim: Among forms written to agree with anomalous readings are variants for 'their omen' and 'his omen on his neck'; the list also includes a variant of 'enter among My servants'.

ITQAN:v3p265/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p265/r1.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p265/r1.claim: Shams al-Din ibn al-Sa'igh catalogs more than forty end-rhyme adjustments, including fronting objects, clauses, temporal phrases, and pronouns; deleting or adding final letters, altering declension, and masculinizing generic nouns.
ITQAN:v3p265/r1.anchor: ألف الشيخ شمس الدين بن الصائغ كتابا سماه إحكام الراي في أحكام الآي قال فيه

ITQAN:v3p265/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p265/r2.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p265/r2.claim: His list says this verse places a clausal modifier before a single-word modifier for the sake of the verse ending.
ITQAN:v3p265/r2.anchor: الخامس تقديم الصفة الجملة على الصفة المفرد نحو

ITQAN:v3p265/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p265/r3.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p265/r3.claim: Other rhyme adjustments he lists include putting the governed word before its governor, putting a later event first, prioritizing the lesser item, and fronting a pronoun before its referent.
ITQAN:v3p265/r3.anchor: أحدها تقديم المعمول إما على العامل نحو

ITQAN:v3p265/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p265/r4.speaker: شمس الدين بن الصائغ
ITQAN:v3p265/r4.claim: He also lists deleting final yā from a definite adjective, an unjussived verb, and an annexed pronoun, and adding long vowels or retaining them with a jussive.
ITQAN:v3p265/r4.anchor: السادس حذف ياء المنقوص المعرف نحو

ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.claim: A Qur’anic pattern pairs the record of deeds shown at judgment with the worldly book of religious rulings that grounds accountability; the Kahf and Isra passages illustrate the pattern.
ITQAN:v3p293#3/r6.anchor: أن عادة القرآن إذا ذكر الكتاب المشتمل على عمل العبد حيث يعرض يوم القيامة أردفه بذكر الكتاب المشتمل على الأحكام الدينية في الدنيا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r1.claim: What readers praise in fluent poetry is apt metaphor, complete ordering that delivers meaning to the heart as wording reaches the ear, and freedom from padding or deficient expression.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r1.anchor: هل تجد لاستحسانهم وحمدهم وثنائهم ومدحهم منصرفا إلا إلى استعارة وقعت موقعها وأصابت غرضها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r2.claim: The poem's opening compresses completion of the pilgrimage rites, fulfillment of obligations and sunnas, and leaving Mina into the general phrase, 'when we had completed every need.'
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r2.anchor: فعبر عن قضاء المناسك بأجمعها والخروج من فروضها وسننها من طريق أمكنة أن يقصر معه اللفظ وهو طريقة العموم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r3.claim: Mentioning someone wiping the corners signals the farewell circumambulation, the final rite, and the departure that is the poem's aim.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p15/r3.anchor: على طواف الوداع الذي هو آخر الأمر ودليل المسير الذي هو مقصوده من الشعر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r1.claim: The poem suppresses understood objects after four verbs, making them seem untransitive and concentrating attention on asserting the actions themselves.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r1.anchor: فيها حذف مفعول مقصود قصده في أربعة مواضع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r2.claim: Leaving the object unexpressed generalizes the effect: a situation of this kind would weary any mother, despite maternal patience; naming ‘us’ would restrict the claim.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r2.anchor: يتضمن أن من حكم مثله في كل أم تمل وتسأم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r3.claim: ‘Chambers that warmed and shaded’ describes chambers whose nature is to provide warmth and shade; adding an explicit object would destroy that general sense.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r3.anchor: حجرات من شأن مثلها أن تدفىء وتظل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r4.claim: The omitted object can convey both focus on the action and a general quality that would be lost if the object were stated.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p130/r4.anchor: توفير العناية على إثبات الفعل ، والدلالة على أن القصد من ذكر الفعل

DAMGHANI:v1p304/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p304/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p304/r2.claim: Ṭāʾir can mean a person’s book or record, including the record of his answer in the grave to Munkar and Nakīr.
DAMGHANI:v1p304/r2.anchor: الثاني الطائر الكتاب قوله سبحانه في سورة الاسراء وكل انسان الزمناه طائره في عنقه يعني كتابه اي كتاب اجابته في القبر لمنكر ونكير

DAMGHANI:v1p304/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p304/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p304/r3.claim: The source also gives ‘fortune and misfortune, good and evil’ as an alternative explanation of a person’s ṭāʾir.

DAMGHANI:v1p335/r8.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r8.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r8.claim: Something fastened to a person’s neck is a metaphor for a burden that remains attached and never leaves him.
DAMGHANI:v1p335/r8.anchor: الثالث في عنقه اي يلزمه كما تلزم القلادة العنق على التمثيل قوله تعالى في سورة الاسراء وكل انسان الزمناه طائره في عنقه

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r1.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r1.claim: An unnamed poet says that even if his hand and self held back, fate would still have its choice over him, supporting the force of destiny.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r1.anchor: ولو ضنت بها كفي ونفسي ... لكان علي للقدر الخيار

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r2.speaker: القس
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r2.claim: Al-Qass says that the paths of misguidance and guidance are apportioned, as the days teach people what they bring.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r2.anchor: وقال القس : قد كنت أعذل في السفاهة أهلها ... فاعجب لما تأتي به الأيام

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r3.speaker: ابن أحمر
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r3.claim: Ibn Ahmar says treatment cannot avert what God has decreed, using حم القدر for fate’s determination.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r3.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر حين سقي بطنه : شربنا وداوينا، وما كان ضرنا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r4.speaker: الشماخ
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r4.claim: Al-Shammakh calls two difficult desires written upon him and glosses مكتوب علي as decreed for him.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r4.anchor: وقال الشماخ : وإني عداني عنكما غير ماقت

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r5.speaker: الأعشى
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r5.claim: Al-Aʿsha says cleverness cannot repel what has been decreed for a person.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r5.anchor: وقال الأعشى : في فتية كسيوف الهند قد علموا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r6.speaker: أبو زبيد
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r6.claim: Abu Zubayd describes a fatal fall that the victim watches helplessly; he explicitly glosses أسبابه as destinies.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r6.anchor: وقال أبو زبيد : فلا تك كالموقوص عن ظهر رحله ... تردت به أسبابه وهو ينظر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r7.speaker: الراعي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r7.claim: Al-Raʿi says a person’s fate was written before birth, and neither a helper nor someone protected from one death is necessarily saved from another.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r7.anchor: وقال الراعي : وهن يحاذرن الردى أن يصيبني ... ومن قبل خلقي خط ما كنت لاقيا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r8.speaker: أفنون التغلبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r8.claim: Afnun al-Taghlibi says a person cannot know how to guard himself unless God appoints a protector for him.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r8.anchor: وقال أفنون التغلبي : لعمرك ما يدري الفتى كيف يتقي ... إذا هو لم يجعل له الله واقيا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r9.claim: Ibn Qutayba rejects glossing Labid’s من شاء أضل as “whomever He names astray”; it means misguiding, a real Arabic sense, not merely labeling someone.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r9.anchor: أفترى لبيدا أراد بقوله: من شاء أضل، أي سمي ضالا؟ لا لعمر الله ما عرف هذا لبيد

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r10.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r10.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p83/r10.claim: Arabic may use الإضلال for destruction because it leads to ruin; ضللنا في الأرض means perished and returned to dust, while water is said to be lost in milk when overwhelmed by it.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r1.claim: The saying أراك بشر ما أحار مشفر describes a camel’s skin and lips as signs of good feeding; أحار means food returned to its stomach.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r1.anchor: وقولهم: أراك بشر ما أحار مشفر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r2.claim: أفلت بجريعة الذقن means someone escaped with his life at the last moment; a Huthali poet depicts the breath at the throat as the person escapes.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r3.claim: The proverb about an immoral woman’s skirt causing consumption means that following promiscuous women wastes one’s wealth; bodily wasting represents financial loss.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r3.anchor: وقولهم: غبار ذيل المرأة الفاجرة يورث السل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r4.claim: كبارح الأروي calls something ill-omened from either direction: mountain goats are considered a bad omen whichever way they come, especially when crossing leftward.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r5.claim: عبد وخلى في يديه describes a lowly, arrogant person who boasts when placed in luxuriant pasture; الخلى means pasture, as a poet says spring growth brings out their hostility.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r6.claim: The saying about spoiled milk and people walking with bows means that abundance can corrupt people and provoke enmity, as the cited verse says hostility sprouts with the spring grass.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r6.anchor: قوم إذا نبت الربيع لهم ... نبتت عداوتهم مع البقل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r7.claim: ترميد means milk descending into the udder; sheep lactate when giving birth, and ربق are loops put on young animals so they cannot follow their mothers to pasture, while goats lactate early in pregnancy and رنق means wait.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r7.anchor: الترميد: نزول اللبن في الضرع. وقولهم في الضأن: أي هي الأرباق

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r8.claim: أفواهها مجاسها means plentiful eating reveals an animal’s fatness, making it unnecessary to feel its body to assess its condition.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r8.anchor: وقولهم: أفواهها مجاسها . يريد: أنها إذا كانت كثيرة الأكل

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r9.claim: In نجارها نارها, نار means a brand mark, and the term applies to anything marked with a cautery iron.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p307/r9.anchor: وقولهم: نجارها نارها . النار هاهنا: السمة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: With prefixed hamza, the perfect follows أفعل and the imperfect follows يفعل; this pattern applies across augmented verbs, with forms like أخرج and يخرج.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: فتلحق أولا ويكون الحرف على أفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Every أفعل follows this pattern as a four-radical verb, whether otherwise augmented or unaugmented; examples include يخرج، تخرج، أخرج, and نخرج.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: كل أفعل فهذا الذي على أربعة أبدا يجرى على مثال يفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Khalil says the expected analogy would retain hamza in the imperfect and related forms, as t is retained in تفعلت and تفاعلت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وزعم الخليل أنه كان القياس أن تثبت الهمزة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Speakers instead regularly delete the hamza in this imperfect pattern because it is heavy and frequent.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: لأن الهمزة تثقل عليهم كما وصفت لك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Deletion is especially apt because the hamza is an added letter attached to an already augmented form, is heavy, and has a replacement when lost.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وكان هذا أجدر أن يحذف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: خطام المجاشعي
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Rajaz poet Khaṭṭām al-Mujāshiʿī retains the hamza under poetic necessity in وصاليات ككما يؤثفين, from أثفيت.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: قال الراجز وهو خطام المجاشعي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: ليلى الأخيلية
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Laylā al-Akhyaliyya likewise retains the hamza under poetic necessity in كرات غلام من كساء مؤرنب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: كرات غلام من كساء مؤرنب

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: For augmented verbs, the agent noun parallels أفعل with mīm replacing initial alif; the object noun follows the imperfect pattern, as in مضروب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: إلا أن موضع الألف ميم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: The مضروب pattern belongs only to unaugmented triliteral roots.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: مثال مضروب فإنه لا يكون

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: No verb takes a prefixed connected hamza as an addition except أفعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: في شيء من الفعل إلا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: An added second radical alif forms فاعل in the perfect and يفاعل in the imperfect, with corresponding patterns for other prefixes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وتلحق الألف ثانية فيكون الحرف على فاعل إذا قلت فعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: The pattern is illustrated by قاتل يقاتل and its related prefixed imperfect forms.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: قاتل يقاتل ويقاتل فأجري مجرى

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Agent and patient nouns from this pattern parallel those from Afʿala if fully formed, despite the different placement of the added alif; examples are قوتل and مقاتل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وذلك قولك قوتل ومقاتل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Nouns from augmented verbs are generally adjectives, except forms on مفعل, which can be lexical nouns such as مخدع.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: إلا ما كان من مفعل فإنه جاء اسما في مخدع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: The second-radical alif occurs in verbs only in the فاعل pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: الألف ثانية في الأفعال إلا في فاعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: An addition at the middle radical produces the فعّل pattern, which follows فاعل across its conjugations, as in جرب يجرب.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: فيكون الحرف على فعل فيجرى في جميع الوجوه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: The imperfect forms with yāʾ, tāʾ, nūn, and hamza follow the same vowel pattern; differing prefixes distinguish their meanings.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وكذلك تفعل ونفعل وأفعل ويجئن كلهن على مثال يفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: These patterns resemble unaugmented quadriliteral verbs such as دحرج in their number of radicals and vowel pattern, which accounts for the prefix vowel and noun formation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: نحو دحرج لأن عدتها كعدتها

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: A prefixed t with فاعل gives تفاعل and يتفاعل; its passive perfect is تفوعل, and its agent and patient nouns use متفاعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: وذلك قولك تغافل يتغافل وتغوفل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: In augmented active and passive participles, the difference is the vowel before the final letter; their initial mīm is always dammated.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: إلا الكسرة التي قبل آخر حرف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: A prefixed t with فعّل follows تفاعل across its inflections, except that its third radical occupies the position corresponding to the long alif.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: إلا أن ثالث ذلك ألف

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.claim: Only تفاعل and تفعل have both an initial t and a third radical addition; تفعل is not given the same prefix vowels because it patterns with quadriliteral تدحرج and has the meaning of انفعل.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابلحاقالزيادةبناتالثلاثةمن.anchor: نحو تكلم ولم تضم زوائد تفعل

NASHR:v2p306/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p306/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر، ويعقوب، وباقي القراء
NASHR:v2p306/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads with yāʾ as a passive form; Yaʿqūb reads with the letter and vowels specified in the text, while the remaining readers use first-person nūn with a kasra on rāʾ.
NASHR:v2p306/r4.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر بالياء وضمها وفتح الراء، وقرأ يعقوب بالباء وفتحها وضم الراء، وقرأ الباقون بالنون وضمها وكسر الراء

NASHR:v2p306/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p306/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p306/r5.claim: All readers put kitāban in the accusative; for Abū Jaʿfar’s passive, the author prefers construing it as a circumstantial accusative, meaning the assigned deed comes out as a book, and applies the same analysis to Yaʿqūb.
NASHR:v2p306/r5.anchor: (واتفقوا) على نصب كتابا ووجه نصبه على قراءة أبي جعفر ونخرج مبنيا للمفعول

NASHR:v2p306/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p306/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر، وابن عامر
NASHR:v2p306/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and Ibn ʿĀmir read with initial ḍamm and a doubled qāf; the rest read with fatḥa and a light qāf.
NASHR:v2p306/r6.anchor: فقرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر بضم الياء وفتح اللام وتشديد القاف، وقرأ الباقون بفتح الياء، وإسكان اللام وتخفيف القاف

NASHR:v2p42/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p42/r1.claim: The excerpt begins mid-discussion of an unspecified form: it records Nafiʿ’s fatḥ, Makki’s preference for fatḥ while reporting both, and al-Shāṭibī’s attribution of both faces to al-Azraq.
NASHR:v2p42/r1.anchor: نافع بالفتح، وكذلك قال: مكي إلا أنه قال: وبالوجهين قرأت

NASHR:v2p42/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p42/r2.claim: Among eleven words where some readers depart from their usual imāla rules, the author lists مزجاة, أتى أمر الله, and يلقاه منشورا, alongside بلى, رأى, أعمى, سوى, سدى, إناه, and نأى.
NASHR:v2p42/r2.anchor: وهي بلى، رأى، مزجاة، أتى أمر الله، يلقاه، أعمى، سوى، سدى، إناه، نأى، رأى

NASHR:v2p42/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r3.speaker: ابن ذكوان
NASHR:v2p42/r3.claim: For مزجاة, أتى أمر الله, and يلقاه, both fatḥ and imāla are sound from Ibn Dhakwān; the author read both through the cited routes and adopts both.
NASHR:v2p42/r3.anchor: وكل من الفتح والإمالة صحيح عن ابن ذكوان في الأحرف الثلاثة قرأنا به من الطرق المذكورة، وبه نأخذ

NASHR:v2p42/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p42/r4.speaker: الصوري
NASHR:v2p42/r4.claim: For يلقاه, al-Ṣūrī reports imāla through the Ramli route; the author also cites al-Dājūnī’s transmission and reports from al-Naqqāsh and Hibat Allāh.
NASHR:v2p42/r4.anchor: وروى عنه إمالة: يلقاه الصوري عن طريق الرملي، وهي رواية الداجوني عن أصحابه عن ابن ذكوان
